The interview should pin down the gap between the last day of SkyVault employment and the first day of PathForge technical work, because that interval is the most readily testable element of the Plaintiff's inference and the one Meridian's own records can corroborate. It also develops the facts relevant to ECIAA Section 7.1, which the Complaint does not plead as a breach but which the Plaintiff could add by amendment.", "purp")

p("Q-A9.  Who joined Meridian from SkyVault, when, and what roles did they take; and describe how you handled recruiting and hiring in the twelve months after you left SkyVault.", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 7.1(a) (no soliciting, recruiting, encouraging or inducing any SkyVault employee to terminate employment) and 7.1(b) (no hiring or engaging any person who is, or was within the six months prior, a SkyVault employee); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 53 (alleging Holt co-founded Meridian with Priya Chandrasekaran in April 2018).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: The Complaint does not plead a non-solicitation breach, but ECIAA Section 7 is in the furnished record and the Plaintiff reserved the right to assert additional theories. Establishing the hiring facts now, from the witness and from Meridian's HR records, prevents an unplanned exposure later. This question is also a document-collection prompt: Meridian's recruiting records and offer letters for 2018-2019 are needed to test the assertion.", "purp")

p("Q-A10.  Describe how you actually spent your working time between February and, say, December 2018 — what you were building, what tools you were using, what you were reading, and where that work product is now.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 1 (\"Developed from the ground up beginning in 2018\") and Section 7.2 timeline (April 2018 incorporation; Q3 2018-Q4 2019 multi-sensor fusion module designed and prototyped); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 54-55 (alleging on information and belief that Holt used misappropriated files to develop PathForge and disclosed SkyVault trade secrets to Meridian engineers).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes an independently corroborable account of the first ten months of PathForge work, which is the period the Complaint treats as unexplained. Because the Plaintiff's case at paras. 54-55 rests on \"information and belief,\" a specific, records-backed account of that period is the most efficient way to displace the inference. The answer also identifies the earliest PathForge artifacts — design notes, notebooks, prototypes, repositories — that should be preserved and collected.", "purp")

p("A.2 — LEAD FAMILY 2: THE PRIOR WORK HOLT DISCLOSED TO SKYVAULT IN 2016", "h2")

p("Q-A11.  I want to go through Exhibit A to your ECIAA with you. Please describe the \"Autonomous Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm\" you listed there — what it did, when you developed it, what became of it, and what relationship it has to the navigation or path-planning work you later did at Meridian.", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A Prior Inventions table, row 1 (\"Autonomous Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm,\" date 2014-2015, \"Developed as part of PhD dissertation research at Georgia Institute of Technology; no patent filed\"), read with Sections 5.3 (exclusion of Prior Inventions listed on Exhibit A from the scope of the Agreement) and 2.1(ii) (Confidential Information excludes information known to Employee prior to disclosure by the Company, as documented by written records); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, recital (PhD in Robotics, Georgia Institute of Technology, 2015).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the content and lineage of the one pre-employment invention Holt affirmatively disclosed, and tests whether the path-planning concepts in that work overlap the PathForge Navigation Module and adaptive path optimization described in the white paper's Section 4.3. If the overlap is real, this is the strongest documentary anchor for the independent-development defense because the disclosure predates the ECIAA by construction. The interview should also identify where the underlying dissertation, code and notes are today.", "purp")

p("Q-A12.  Describe the \"RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit\" you listed on Exhibit A — what it did, why you published it, under what license, who else used it, and whether any part of it found its way into PathForge.", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A Prior Inventions table, row 2 (\"RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit (open-source),\" 2015, \"Published on GitHub under MIT License; available at github.com/mholt-robotics/robonav-cal\"), read with Sections 5.3 and 2.1(iv) (Confidential Information excludes information disclosed to Employee by a third party not under a confidentiality obligation to the Company); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 3.2 Step 3 (Pre-Processing and Noise Filtering, including sensor calibration correction) and Section 3.3 (attributing benchmark improvements to \"commercial-grade sensor calibration\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes a documented, publicly licensed body of Holt's own prior work that is directly adjacent to an accused PathForge capability (sensor calibration within the fusion pipeline). This supports the independent-development and prior-work defenses and simultaneously identifies the MIT-licensed codebase whose commit history and license file can be independently verified. The question also begins the attribution analysis for any third-party or open-source component that may be present in PathForge, which is a separate and independent development story from SkyVault.", "purp")

p("Q-A13.  When you signed Exhibit A on June 13, 2016, was the list complete as far as you understood it? Were there any other prior inventions, tools, codebases or publications of yours that you considered but decided not to list?", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A Prior Inventions Disclosure, final paragraph (\"If no Prior Inventions are listed above, Employee represents that there are no Prior Inventions to disclose\") and the employee initials \"M.H.\" and date June 13, 2016; holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 5.3 (Exclusions) and Section 9.3 (Entire Agreement).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests the completeness of the 2016 disclosure, which is both a defensive asset and a potential exposure: if Holt had other prior work he failed to list, the Plaintiff will characterize that as concealment, and if he had none, the two listed items are the full universe of pre-employment technology he can claim. This also lays groundwork for identifying additional prior publications (papers, conference talks, repositories) that may independently pre-date or anticipate the accused functionality.", "purp")

p("Q-A14.  Describe any work you did on autonomous navigation, sensor fusion or path planning between 2015 and June 2016, before you joined SkyVault, and identify any documents, publications or repositories from that period.", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 2.1(ii) (information known to Employee prior to disclosure by the Company, as documented by written records, is excluded from Confidential Information) and Section 3.4 (preservation of general skills, knowledge, experience and expertise, and the right to use publicly available information and general industry knowledge); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A Prior Inventions table (both rows dated 2014-2015 and 2015).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Fills the one-year gap between the Exhibit A entries and the June 2016 start date, and identifies the written records that ECIAA Section 2.1(ii) requires if prior knowledge is to be excluded from Confidential Information. Because that exclusion is conditioned on documentation, this question is as much a document-collection task as a factual one, and the answer determines whether the exclusion is available at all.", "purp")

p("A.3 — LEAD FAMILY 3: THE TRUE DEVELOPMENT STARTING POINT FOR EACH PATHFORGE MODULE", "h2")

p("Q-A15.  Take me module by module. For the multi-sensor fusion and obstacle avoidance capability: when did design work actually begin, who worked on it, and what did the first version look like?", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 1 (three core technology pillars) and Section 7.2 timeline bullet (Q3 2018-Q4 2019: multi-sensor fusion module designed and prototyped; architecture informed by review of published literature including Vasquez (2016) and Nakamura and Okonkwo (2015)); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Sections 3.1-3.3 (sensor suite, extended Kalman filter framework, seven-stage pipeline, performance benchmarks); skyvault-complaint.docx, claim chart table for the '561 Patent, claim 1 (mapping claim limitations to PathForge's \"Sensor Integration Layer,\" \"Threat Assessment Module,\" \"Dynamic Path Replanner\" and \"Flight Controller API\"); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 27-28, 65-68 (the '561 Patent, filed March 14, 2017, naming Dr. Rajan Mehta as sole inventor).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Separates a single accused capability into its constituent technical modules so that each can be traced to its own origin. The Complaint's claim chart treats the fusion pillar as one feature set; the white paper's Section 7.2 timeline asserts a Q3 2018-Q4 2019 development window that begins after Holt left SkyVault. The interview must establish which specific components existed when, because a module-by-module chronology is the only way to test the Plaintiff's timeline inference and to allocate the defense between independent development, prior art, and non-infringement.", "purp")

p("Q-A16.  Same question for the GPS-denied navigation and adaptive path optimization capability: when did that work begin, who did it, and what was the first working version?", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.2 timeline bullet (Q1 2019-Q3 2020: GPS-denied navigation module developed; design informed by academic visual-inertial odometry research and publicly available implementations including the DroneNav open-source project (2017)); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Sections 4.2-4.4 (VIO pipeline, sliding-window optimization, keyframe-based map management, IMU pre-integration, adaptive flight path optimization, GPS-denied performance table); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 29 and 75-77 (the '227 Patent, filed November 9, 2018, naming Dr. Rajan Mehta and Dr. Anita Venkatesh).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests the white paper's own timeline against the witness's recollection and against records. The asserted Q1 2019 start is significant because the '227 Patent was filed November 9, 2018, so the chronology matters to both the derivation theory and any independent-development narrative. This question also identifies the specific PathForge code that corresponds to the accused \"Dynamic Path Replanner\" and \"adaptive flight path optimization\" features, which is the code that will eventually have to be compared to the AeroCore files named in the Complaint.", "purp")

p("Q-A17.  Same question for the swarm coordination and communication capability: when did it begin, who worked on it, and how did the protocol design evolve?", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 5.1 (\"The swarm module was developed beginning in 2019, with first production deployment in early 2021\") and Section 7.2 timeline bullet (Q2 2019-Q1 2021: swarm coordination protocol designed and tested; protocol design based on published distributed systems and MANET research, including consensus algorithms for multi-robot coordination (Ferreira et al., 2016)); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Sections 5.2-5.4 (mesh networking at 900 MHz or 2.4 GHz, low-latency message protocol, heartbeat broadcasts, decentralized consensus, priority-based deconfliction, scalability results); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 30 and 82-86 (the '889 Patent, filed June 22, 2020, naming Dr. Rajan Mehta, Dr. Anita Venkatesh and Kevin Larsson).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Isolates the swarm module, which the white paper itself describes as an independent engineering effort with its own start date and its own literature base. Because the '889 Patent was filed June 22, 2020 — after PathForge's September 2020 launch but within the asserted swarm development window — the timing of the swarm work is unusually consequential and should be documented with commit and release records rather than recollection alone.", "purp")

p("Q-A18.  For each module, identify the actual source code: the repository, the file names, who authored the initial versions, and what third-party or open-source dependencies were brought in. I am looking for a list I can use to request the records.", "q")
p("Source: skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 33 and 116 (identifying the AeroCore source files `navfusion.c`, `pathoptengine.h` and `swarm_proto.cpp`) and paras. 118-120 (alleging that PathForge firmware contains substantially similar code, including in \"structure, sequence, and organization\"); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 61(iii) (demanding \"a full forensic audit of Meridian's source code repositories\"); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 15 (declining to provide access to source code repositories for any forensic audit, calling the demand premature, overbroad and without legal basis outside formal litigation with protective measures).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: This is the single most important document-collection question in the interview. The Complaint's copyright count names three AeroCore files but asserts similarity in the abstract; the answer identifies the PathForge counterparts by repository, path and author so that a technical comparison can be scoped, sequenced and performed under protective order rather than argued from the white paper. It also frames the response to the Plaintiff's audit demand recorded at Complaint para. 61(iii) and refused at April 5 Response para. 15.", "purp")

p("Q-A19.  Describe the software development practices at Meridian in the 2018-2021 period — version control, code review, dependency management, licensing review, testing and release records — and tell me which of those records still exist and where.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.1 (modules \"independently developed, independently deployable, and independently priced\") and Section 7.2 final paragraph (\"All PathForge technology was developed independently by the Meridian engineering team\"); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (\"Meridian independently developed its PathForge platform through the efforts of its engineering teams\" and \"maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property\"); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 118-119 (alleging copying of code and asserting that the similarities \"cannot be explained by independent creation\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Converts the April 5 Response's unsworn independent-development and compliance representations into verifiable practice, and identifies the records that would corroborate them. The Complaint's assertion at para. 119 that the similarities cannot be explained by independent creation is testable only against contemporaneous development records, so locating those records — and establishing now whether any have been lost — is essential before the representation is repeated in a filing or a deposition.", "purp")

p("Q-A20.  Were any portions of the PathForge platform, or any predecessor prototype, written by anyone outside Meridian — contractors, consultants, academic collaborators, or a predecessor entity — and if so, who and under what terms?", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 2.1(iv) (Confidential Information excludes information disclosed to Employee by a third party not under a confidentiality obligation to the Company); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 2 (describing DroneNav and academic literature as influences on the design) and Section 7.2 (describing review of published academic literature during prototyping); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (asserting independent development by Meridian's engineering teams).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Identifies any third-party contribution to PathForge, which is a distinct and independent development story and a potential source of additional prior-art or ownership facts. It also protects against the risk that the \"developed independently by the Meridian engineering team\" representation is inaccurate in a respect Meridian has not yet checked, and it identifies the individuals whose records and agreements should be collected.", "purp")

p("Q-A21.  Exhibit F records six bulk exports from SkyVault's Confluence workspace in the week before your last day, including 84 files from the /SkyVault/Business/CustomerData/ space. Describe what you understood those files to be, what you intended to do with them, and whether any SkyVault-origin file has ever been present on any Meridian system, device or account.", "q")
p("Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Rows #27-#32 (six BULK_EXPORT events, 02/02/2018 through 02/08/2018, including Row #32 on 02/08/2018 at 22:44:06 UTC / 04:44:06 PM CT, 84 files, 467.2 MB, from /SkyVault/Business/CustomerData/ to Local Disk C:\\Users\\mholt\\Downloads\\export_020818b, flagged \"User exported files from Business/CustomerData space — outside normal Engineering scope\"), Row #17 (FILE_VIEW of customer_contracts_summary_2017.xlsx on 01/24/2018, flagged \"User accessed Business/CustomerData space — outside normal Engineering scope\"), and Row #34 (the 02/09/2018 BULK_COPY_TO_REMOVABLE spanning /SkyVault/Engineering/ and /SkyVault/Business/CustomerData/); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 49 (alleging on information and belief that the download included all five trade secret categories including customer lists and pricing strategies) and para. 94 (same, in the DTSA count).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Confronts the most damaging documentary fact in the furnished record directly and early, on the witness's own terms, rather than leaving it to be raised at a deposition. The distinction the interview must develop is between files that were viewed or exported and files that were used or retained; Exhibit F proves the former and is silent on the latter. The customer-data exports are also the factual basis for the TS-3 category, so the answer determines whether that category is genuinely in the case or is unsupported.", "purp")

p("A.4 — LEAD FAMILY 4: THE WHITE PAPER'S TITLE AND AUTHORSHIP INFORMATION", "h2")

p("Q-A22.  Turning to the July 2022 PathForge white paper: tell me how that document came to be written, who decided to write it, who drafted which sections, and what role you played.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, cover page (title \"PathForge: Next-Generation Autonomous Navigation,\" dated July 2022, attributed to \"Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder\" and \"PathForge Engineering Team,\" Meridian Dynamics, Inc., 900 Lakeshore Drive, Floor 12, Austin, TX 78701); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 57 (alleging the white paper was published in or about July 2022 and \"authored by Dr. Marcus Holt and the Meridian engineering team\") and para. 58 (alleging the white paper describes PathForge's technical architecture in detail).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the authorship and genesis of the document that SkyVault says triggered its discovery of the alleged misappropriation (Complaint paras. 97 and 109: \"SkyVault first discovered the misappropriation of its trade secrets upon reviewing Meridian's PathForge white paper published in or about July 2022\"). Authorship matters twice over: it determines whose statements the document contains, and it frames the limitations-period and notice chronology that SkyVault itself has pleaded. The answer also identifies the internal drafting and review records, which are the best evidence of the document's intended character.", "purp")

p("Q-A23.  Exhibit F and the Complaint both put weight on the Confluence content Holt could reach. The white paper is a public document. What was the intended audience for the white paper, and was any part of it reviewed or cleared before release?", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, cover page (\"Document Classification: Public Release / Marketing Technical Paper\") and the notice at the end of the document (\"© 2022 Meridian Dynamics, Inc. All rights reserved. This white paper is provided for informational purposes. The technical descriptions herein represent PathForge capabilities as of the date of publication (July 2022) and are subject to change. PathForge White Paper v1.0 — July 2022\"); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 58 and 77 (relying on the white paper as describing PathForge's architecture and its GPS-denied navigation module in terms corresponding to the asserted patents).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the document's purpose and audience so that its weight can be accurately assessed. Because the Complaint relies on the white paper as its principal technical evidence (paras. 58, 77, 85), the defense needs a clear record that the document is a marketing characterization of capability, not a design specification, and that its statements are qualified on their face. The internal review record will show who approved the technical claims and on what basis.", "purp")

p("Q-A24.  Section 7.2 of the white paper states that \"All PathForge technology was developed independently by the Meridian engineering team.\" When that sentence was drafted, what was it based on — what records, reviews or verification? And separately, Section 2 says you \"led the PathForge architecture design\" drawing on a \"thorough review of the published literature.\" Describe that literature review: what you read, when, and how it was recorded.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.2 final paragraph (\"All PathForge technology was developed independently by the Meridian engineering team. The platform builds upon publicly available academic research and open-source implementations that are widely known in the autonomous systems community.\") and Section 2 (\"Dr. Marcus Holt, who holds a PhD in Robotics from Georgia Institute of Technology (2015), led the PathForge architecture design, drawing on his extensive academic background in autonomous systems and a thorough review of the published literature\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests the foundation of the independent-development representation before it is repeated in a sworn filing. A representation made in a 2022 marketing paper and repeated in an April 2024 litigation letter carries different risk if it was never grounded in a documented review. This question is also a document-collection prompt for any literature review memoranda, reading lists, citation records or design documents from 2018-2019.", "purp")

p("Q-A25.  The white paper attributes specific technical approaches to third parties — Vasquez (2016), Nakamura and Okonkwo (2015), and the DroneNav project (2017). For each, tell me whether you personally read the work, when, and whether any of its code, formulas or design choices were used in PathForge.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 2 (describing Vasquez, \"Multi-Sensor Fusion for Autonomous UAV Navigation,\" IEEE Transactions on Robotics, Vol. 32, No. 5, October 2016, as \"a foundational contribution\" establishing LiDAR/stereo/IMU fusion through an extended Kalman filter framework, and DroneNav as validating sliding-window optimization and keyframe-based map management); Section 3.3 (comparing PathForge's 38 ms and 8 cm results to Vasquez's 47 ms and 15 cm, and describing PathForge's approach as \"a commercially optimized implementation of that foundational methodology\"); Section 3.1 (\"follows the general approach established by Vasquez (2016)\"); Section 4.2 and 4.3 (DroneNav as the demonstrated basis for sliding-window VIO); Section 5.2 (Ferreira et al., 2016 for consensus algorithms); and the References list (four items, including the DroneNav GitHub repository at https://github.com/dronenav/dronenav, first committed August 15, 2017).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Pins the independent-development narrative to named, publicly verifiable sources and distinguishes between the different relationships a witness can have to a public source. The white paper's own citations are the best evidence that PathForge's design was grounded in public literature rather than in SkyVault material, but only if the witness can describe the actual use of each source — read, cited, evaluated, cloned, imported as a dependency, modified, or not used at all. This question should be asked separately for each of Vasquez (2016), Nakamura and Okonkwo (2015), DroneNav (2017) and Ferreira et al. (2016), and the answers should be documented individually.", "purp")

p("A.5 — LEAD FAMILY 5: DRONENAV AND OTHER PUBLIC SOURCES", "h2")

p("Q-A26.  Focusing on DroneNav: tell me what you know about that project, when you first became aware of it, whether you or anyone at Meridian ever cloned, downloaded, forked or imported its code, and whether any DroneNav code is present in PathForge today.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 2 (DroneNav project, GitHub, first committed August 15, 2017, described as \"an early open-source implementation of visual-inertial odometry for GPS-denied drone flight\" whose \"publicly available codebase provided a valuable reference point\"), Section 4.1 (\"significant prior work including the DroneNav open-source project (2017)\"), Section 4.2 (\"Open-source implementations such as the DroneNav project (2017) have demonstrated the viability of sliding-window VIO for GPS-denied UAV flight. DroneNav's publicly available codebase implemented the core pipeline of feature tracking, sliding-window optimization, keyframe management, and IMU pre-integration for monocular camera configurations\"), Section 7.2 timeline (design informed by \"publicly available implementations including the DroneNav open-source project (2017)\"), and the References list item 2 (URL https://github.com/dronenav/dronenav).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: This question separates the distinct relationships a witness can have to a public codebase — awareness, citation, evaluation, cloning, dependency inclusion, modification, use, and non-use — because the legal significance of each is different and the white paper's language (\"reference point,\" \"informed by\") is deliberately imprecise. Note the timing fact that must be tested: DroneNav's first commit is dated August 15, 2017, which is during Holt's SkyVault employment, so the interview should establish whether he encountered it at SkyVault or only later at Meridian. The answer determines whether the GPS-denied module has an independent open-source lineage that can be demonstrated by commit history and license records.", "purp")

p("Q-A27.  Beyond DroneNav, describe every other public source — open-source project, published paper, standard, vendor SDK or public dataset — that contributed to PathForge, and identify the license and the specific contribution of each.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, References list (Vasquez 2016; DroneNav 2017; Nakamura and Okonkwo 2015; Ferreira, dos Santos and Patel, \"Consensus Algorithms for Decentralized Multi-Robot Coordination,\" ICRA 2016, pp. 4421-4428); Section 2 (\"the state of the art ... was characterized by a rich body of academic research and early open-source implementations\"); Section 3.3 (attributing PathForge's performance gains to \"engineering investment in commercial-grade sensor calibration, noise modeling, and processing pipeline optimization\"); Section 5.4 (attributing sub-linear scaling to the mesh topology architectural choice); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 3.4 (right to use publicly available information and general industry knowledge) and Section 2.1(i) (Confidential Information excludes information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault or breach by Employee).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Builds the affirmative provenance record for each PathForge module from public sources, which is the factual core of both the independent-development defense and the ECIAA Section 2.1(i) and 3.4 carve-outs. The white paper names only four references across a 42-page technical document, so the interview should test whether that list is exhaustive or illustrative; a complete inventory with licenses will also be needed for any open-source compliance analysis.", "purp")

p("Q-A28.  For each module, describe the modifications Meridian made to the public approaches it adopted — what was changed, why, and who did the work — and identify the records that document those changes.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 4.2 final paragraph (identifying three specific engineering improvements to the VIO pipeline: multi-scale feature tracking for low-texture environments, adaptive keyframe selection based on information gain, and tightly-coupled LiDAR-VIO fusion as a fallback mode) and Section 4.3 (extending VIO-based navigation \"by integrating mission-level planning with real-time localization uncertainty\"); Section 3.3 (19% latency improvement and 47% accuracy improvement over the Vasquez baseline, attributed to calibration, noise modeling and pipeline optimization); Section 1 final paragraph (\"The platform's value lies in its unique integration, optimization, and commercial-grade implementation of these techniques\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the specific incremental contributions that Meridian claims as its own, which is what distinguishes an independently developed platform from a copy of a public one and from a derivative of SkyVault code. The white paper already identifies three concrete VIO improvements and one planning extension; the interview should test whether those were actually implemented, when, by whom, and whether the corresponding design documents, pull requests and test results exist. This is the evidence that answers the Complaint's assertion at para. 119 that the asserted similarities \"cannot be explained by independent creation.\"", "purp")

p("A.6 — LEAD FAMILY 6: THE PRE-SUIT CORRESPONDENCE CHAIN", "h2")

p("Q-A29.  Tell me what you recall about the March 2024 correspondence from SkyVault's counsel — when you first learned of it, what you were told about it, and what you did in response.", "q")
p("Source: skyvault-complaint.docx para. 61 (alleging that on March 12, 2024 SkyVault through Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP sent a cease-and-desist letter addressed to Priya Chandrasekaran, CEO, at Meridian's Austin headquarters, identifying the '561, '227 and '889 Patents and SkyVault's trade secret and copyright claims, and demanding cessation, $15 million in licensing fees, and a full forensic audit of Meridian's source code repositories); meridian-cd-response.docx, first paragraph (acknowledging receipt of \"your March 12, 2024 letter sent on behalf of SkyVault Technologies LLC\" and stating the letter is written \"on behalf of Meridian and its officers and directors\"); meridian-cd-response.docx, addressee line (letter addressed to Theresa N. Voss, Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP) and cc line (Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian Dynamics, Inc., via email).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the discoverable chronology of notice, which is the predicate for the willful-infringement allegations at Complaint paras. 63, 69-70, 78 and 86, and for the trade secret and copyright willfulness allegations. Note the limits of the furnished record: the March 12, 2024 letter itself was not provided, so nothing beyond what Complaint para. 61 and the April 5 Response record may be attributed to it, and the interview should ask the witness to identify and produce Meridian's copy of the letter rather than assume its contents. The question also identifies who at Meridian received, read and acted on the letter — a factual matter distinct from any privileged advice about it.", "purp")

p("Q-A30.  After Meridian received the March 2024 letter, describe what happened operationally at the company — any instruction about documents, devices, repositories or communications; any change to how records were kept; and any direction about who could speak about the matter.", "q")
p("Source: meridian-cd-response.docx paras. 10-16 (Meridian's denial of the patent, trade secret and copyright allegations; assertion of independent development; reservation of non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability and independent-development defenses; and declination of all three demands, including the source code audit at para. 15) and para. 18 (request that SkyVault route future communications to Brackwell & Haines and refrain from contacting Meridian's officers and employees directly); exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Rows #40, #41 and #45 (showing, in the analogous 2018 SkyVault sequence, an exit interview scheduled, a permissions audit initiated, and a forensic image requested \"per counsel authorization\" — a useful comparator for what a documented preservation response looks like).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: This question is deliberately framed to elicit discoverable operational facts — instructions, retention changes, preservation steps — and not privileged advice. The scope and adequacy of Meridian's preservation response is a facts-and-conduct issue that will be litigated independently of the merits, and it is better to establish the record now than to reconstruct it later. The 2018 SkyVault entries in Exhibit F are included as a comparator precisely because they show what a contemporaneous, documented hold response looks like on the other side.", "purp")

p("Q-A31.  The April 5, 2024 response states that Meridian \"maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property.\" From your vantage point as CTO, describe those processes as they existed in 2018-2019 when PathForge was being built, and tell me what has changed since.", "q")
p("Source: meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (\"Meridian independently developed its PathForge platform through the efforts of its engineering teams and respects the intellectual property rights of others. Meridian maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property.\"); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 4.2 (approval requirement for personal storage devices) and 5.1 (invention disclosure obligation), as an example of the kind of control the representation describes; pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.1 (independent development, deployment and pricing of modules) and Section 7.2 final paragraph (independent development assertion).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests an unsworn representation that Meridian may later need to defend, and does so while there is still time to correct or qualify it. The question distinguishes the compliance program as it existed when the accused development occurred from the program as it exists today, because a representation about present processes cannot be used to establish past conduct. The answer also identifies the documents — policies, training records, onboarding materials, license review procedures — that would substantiate the representation if it is accurate.", "purp")

p("Q-A32.  What did you understand SkyVault to be asserting about the relationship between your SkyVault work and PathForge, and what do you say in response — specifically, what did you take, what did you use, and what did you not take or use?", "q")
p("Source: skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 2, 54-55 and 119-120 (alleging on information and belief that Holt used SkyVault's proprietary technology and copyrighted firmware to build PathForge, that he disclosed trade secrets to Meridian engineers, and that he copied, modified or incorporated AeroCore source code); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (denying the trade secret and copyright allegations \"in their entirety\" and asserting independent development); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 16 (reserving non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability and independent-development defenses).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Obtains the witness's own denial in his own words, in a privileged setting, before it is tested in a deposition, and forces the answer to be specific rather than categorical. The Complaint's central allegations against Holt are pleaded \"on information and belief,\" so a concrete, itemized account of what he did and did not take or use is the most useful thing this interview can produce. Counsel should record the answer verbatim and should resist the temptation to help the witness characterize it.", "purp")
PYEOF
python3 -c "exec(open('/tmp/memo/part2.py').read()); print('part2 items:', len(CONTENT))"",
  "description": "Write memo part 2 (Holt questions)"
}

{
  "command": "cat > /tmp/memo/part3.py <<'PYEOF'
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# Part 3: Category B - Meridian technical team
CONTENT = []
def p(t="", k="body"): CONTENT.append((k, t))

p("V. CATEGORY B — MERIDIAN TECHNICAL TEAM", "h1")
p("Function in this round. The technical witnesses exist to supply what Dr. Holt cannot supply alone: a module-by-module, author-level account of how PathForge was actually built, given by the people who did the work rather than by the executive who directed it. Their testimony is the only route to the repository, build, dependency, test and release records that will either corroborate or contradict the independent-development position asserted in the July 2022 white paper and the April 5, 2024 response, and it is the only route to identifying the PathForge source files that correspond to the three AeroCore files named in the Complaint. The interviews should be conducted engineer by engineer and module by module, not as a group, and the sequence below is designed so that each witness is asked first what they personally did, then what they observed others do, and only then what they understood about third-party or SkyVault-origin material. Counsel should confirm at the outset that each witness has been told the interview is privileged, that they should not speculate, and that a \"I don't recall\" or \"I would need to check the repository\" answer is more useful than a confident reconstruction.", "body")

p("B.1 — LEAD FAMILY 3 (CONTINUED): PATHFORGE'S ACTUAL DEVELOPMENT STARTING POINT", "h2")

p("Q-B1.  Describe when you joined Meridian, what you were hired to work on, and the first thing you were asked to build. If you can, give me the month and year you started on each component you have worked on.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.2 timeline (April 2018 incorporation and start of PathForge development under Holt's technical leadership; Q3 2018-Q4 2019 fusion module; Q1 2019-Q3 2020 GPS-denied navigation module; Q2 2019-Q1 2021 swarm coordination protocol; September 2020 PathForge v1.0 launch; Q1 2021 swarm production deployment; Q3 2021 analytics dashboard release) and Section 1 (engineering team of approximately 45 working full-time on PathForge development and customer integration); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 12 (alleging approximately 112 Meridian employees) and para. 56 (alleging the September 2020 launch).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Builds an independent, person-by-person chronology that can be checked against the white paper's published timeline and against repository metadata. Because the Complaint's misappropriation theory depends substantially on the asserted speed of PathForge development (paras. 54 and 140), a witness-level timeline is the most direct rebuttal available and does not depend on Holt's credibility.", "purp")

p("Q-B2.  For the module you know best, walk me through the first working version: what it did, what it did not do, and what the immediate predecessor was. If it was derived from something that already existed, tell me what that something was.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.1 (PathForge is \"a modular platform consisting of multiple distinct technology components\" that are \"independently developed, independently deployable, and independently priced\") and Section 5.1 (swarm module developed beginning in 2019 with first production deployment in early 2021); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Sections 3.1 (EKF framework), 4.2 (VIO pipeline components) and 5.2 (mesh networking, low-latency message protocol, heartbeat broadcasts, decentralized consensus) as the module descriptions to test against.", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the true starting point of each module from the person who built it. This is the factual question that decides whether the accused functionality was independently developed, adapted from public sources, or derived from SkyVault material, and it cannot be answered from the white paper because the white paper asserts a starting point without documenting one.", "purp")

p("Q-B3.  Identify the repositories, branches and file paths for the components you worked on, and tell me who authored the initial commit for each. I want names and paths, not descriptions.", "q")
p("Source: skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 33 and 116 (naming AeroCore source files `navfusion.c`, `pathoptengine.h` and `swarm_proto.cpp`), para. 118 (alleging PathForge firmware contains code substantially similar to those files) and para. 61(iii) (demanding a full forensic audit of Meridian's source code repositories); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 15 (declining the audit demand as premature and overbroad and stating that such access would require formal litigation with appropriate protective measures); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.1 (four independently deployable modules).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Produces the concrete inventory needed to scope a source-code comparison and to respond to the audit demand on Meridian's own terms. The Complaint asserts similarity at the level of \"structure, sequence, and organization\" without identifying a single PathForge file, so the defense must build the file-level map itself. This question also supports a proportionate production proposal under a protective order, which is a materially stronger position than the blanket refusal recorded in the April 5 Response.", "purp")

p("Q-B4.  Describe the architecture of the module you worked on — how it is structured internally and how it interfaces with the other modules — and tell me whether any part of it was written by reusing code from another project, inside or outside Meridian.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.1 (each module \"was engineered as a self-contained component with well-defined interfaces\") and Section 3.2 (the seven-stage pipeline: sensor data acquisition, temporal alignment, pre-processing and noise filtering, EKF fusion, 3D occupancy grid generation, obstacle classification and tracking, avoidance path computation); skyvault-complaint.docx, claim chart table for the '561 Patent, claim 1 (mapping claim limitations to PathForge's Sensor Integration Layer, Threat Assessment Module, Dynamic Path Replanner and Flight Controller API).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests the modularity representation in the white paper against the actual code structure, and identifies reuse that may originate from a third party rather than from SkyVault. The Complaint's claim chart treats PathForge as an integrated accused product; if the modules are genuinely independent, that fact affects both the technical comparison and any apportionment of damages.", "purp")

p("Q-B5.  Exhibit F, which SkyVault filed with its Complaint, records a transfer of approximately 4,700 files to a removable USB device on February 9, 2018 and six bulk exports from the Confluence workspace in the preceding week. Based on your own knowledge of Meridian's systems, is there any SkyVault-origin file, document or data set in any Meridian repository, file share, device or account that you are aware of?", "q")
p("Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Rows #27-#32 (six BULK_EXPORT events from 02/02/2018 to 02/08/2018, 1,526 files, approximately 9,681 MB, including 84 files from /SkyVault/Business/CustomerData/) and Row #34 (BULK_COPY_TO_REMOVABLE on 02/09/2018, 4,700 files, 18,473.2 MB, to Removable Disk F:\\SkyVault_Export\\, flagged ALERT); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 48-50 and 94 (alleging the download and that it included files containing all five trade secret categories) and para. 119 (alleging Holt had access to and copied AeroCore source code); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (denying the trade secret and copyright allegations in their entirety).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests the denial at the systems level with the witnesses who would actually know. This is the question that determines whether Meridian can support a clean-hands factual position on the retained-files issue, and it identifies the systems and custodians whose records should be searched. Counsel should be alert that a negative answer from one engineer does not establish a company-wide negative, so the question should be asked of every technical witness and paired with a records search.", "purp")

p("B.2 — LEAD FAMILY 5 (CONTINUED): PUBLIC SOURCES, DEPENDENCIES AND THEIR ACTUAL USE", "h2")

p("Q-B6.  I want to go through each public source named in the white paper with you one at a time. For each, tell me whether you personally read, cited, evaluated, cloned, imported as a dependency, modified, used, or did not use it.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, References list (E. Vasquez, \"Multi-Sensor Fusion for Autonomous UAV Navigation,\" IEEE Transactions on Robotics, Vol. 32, No. 5, pp. 1142-1158, October 2016; DroneNav Project, GitHub, first committed August 15, 2017, https://github.com/dronenav/dronenav; T. Nakamura and S. Okonkwo, \"Extended Kalman Filter Design for Multi-Sensor UAV State Estimation,\" Journal of Autonomous Robotics, Vol. 14, No. 3, pp. 287-305, 2015; L. Ferreira, R. dos Santos and K. Patel, \"Consensus Algorithms for Decentralized Multi-Robot Coordination,\" ICRA 2016, pp. 4421-4428) read with Section 2 (describing Vasquez as \"a foundational contribution\" and DroneNav as validating sliding-window optimization and keyframe-based map management), Section 3.1 and 3.3 (PathForge's approach \"follows the general approach established by Vasquez (2016)\" and represents \"a commercially optimized implementation of that foundational methodology\"), Section 4.2 (DroneNav's codebase \"implemented the core pipeline\" of the VIO approach), Section 5.2 (Ferreira et al. for consensus) and Section 7.2 (design \"informed by\" Vasquez and Nakamura and Okonkwo, and \"informed by\" DroneNav).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Forces the distinction between the different relationships a witness can have to a public source, because the white paper's verbs (\"informed,\" \"reference point,\" \"follows the general approach\") are not precise enough to establish independent development or to exclude copying. A dependency that was cloned and modified is a different fact from a paper that was read, and both are different from a source that was named for credibility and never used. The answer should be recorded source by source, with the witness's own recollection of when they encountered each one.", "purp")

p("Q-B7.  For DroneNav specifically: who on the team worked with it, what was actually taken from it if anything, and how can we demonstrate today what was and was not taken?", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 4.2 (DroneNav's codebase \"implemented the core pipeline of feature tracking, sliding-window optimization, keyframe management, and IMU pre-integration for monocular camera configurations\" and PathForge \"builds upon these established techniques with several engineering improvements\") and Section 7.2 (PathForge's VIO pipeline \"was developed independently, drawing on the same well-known algorithmic foundations — sliding-window optimization, keyframe-based mapping, IMU pre-integration — while adding\" the three named improvements); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 2 (DroneNav first committed August 15, 2017; described as a proof-of-concept whose codebase \"provided a valuable reference point for the broader community\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: DroneNav is the pivotal public source for the GPS-denied module and the one most likely to be probed at a deposition, because its first commit date falls inside Holt's SkyVault tenure and because the white paper describes its pipeline in the same component terms the '227 Patent claims. The interview should establish the mechanics of any use — clone, fork, vendored copy, dependency declaration, or reading only — and should identify the artifacts (repository history, license file, package manifests, build scripts, design notes) that will prove the answer independently.", "purp")

p("Q-B8.  List every third-party or open-source component in the module you worked on, with its license, and tell me whether any of them was modified and whether the modifications were contributed back or documented.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 1 final paragraph (the platform's value lies in \"its unique integration, optimization, and commercial-grade implementation of these techniques\") and Section 7.2 final paragraph (\"The platform builds upon publicly available academic research and open-source implementations that are widely known in the autonomous systems community\"); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 3.4 (the right to use publicly available information and general industry knowledge) and Section 2.1(i) (Confidential Information excludes information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault or breach by Employee); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (\"Meridian maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Builds the component-level provenance record that supports both the independent-development defense and the representation about compliance processes, and it is the record that would be needed for any open-source license analysis. The white paper's four references cannot be the whole inventory of a platform this size, so the interview should treat the published list as a starting point and ask for the complete dependency record.", "purp")

p("Q-B9.  Describe the specific improvements Meridian made to the public approaches it adopted — multi-scale feature tracking, adaptive keyframe selection, and LiDAR-VIO fusion — and tell me who built each, when, and what records document the work.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 4.2 final paragraph (identifying exactly three engineering improvements: (1) multi-scale feature tracking for low-texture environments, (2) adaptive keyframe selection based on information gain rather than fixed temporal or spatial intervals, and (3) tightly-coupled LiDAR-VIO fusion as a fallback mode for featureless corridors or low-light conditions) and Section 4.3 (PathForge's implementation \"extends the foundational VIO-based navigation demonstrated in projects like DroneNav by integrating mission-level planning with real-time localization uncertainty\"); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 119 (asserting that the similarities \"cannot be explained by independent creation\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: The white paper already identifies the precise incremental contributions Meridian claims; the interview converts those claims into evidence by attaching each to an author, a date and a record. These four items are the most concrete available answer to the Complaint's assertion that independent creation cannot explain the asserted similarities, and they should be documented before any technical comparison is performed so that the comparison is measured against a specific account of what Meridian added.", "purp")

p("Q-B10.  Where do PathForge's performance numbers come from? The white paper reports 99.7% detection rate, 38 ms latency, 8 cm accuracy, under 0.5% drift, 97.3% mission completion, 14 ms inter-drone latency, zero collisions across 1,200+ hours and scalability to 24 drones. Identify the test records behind those numbers.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 3.3 performance benchmark table and the accompanying comparison to Vasquez (2016) (47 ms latency and 15 cm accuracy in controlled laboratory conditions; PathForge's 19% latency improvement and 47% accuracy improvement in structured environments; 14 cm RMS in unstructured environments); Section 4.4 performance table and the description of testing environments (a 10,000 sq. ft. warehouse, a 1.2-kilometer utility tunnel, a simulated urban canyon course with building separations of 8-15 meters); Section 5.4 performance table; Section 8 conclusion (restating the same figures); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 58 and 77 (relying on the white paper to describe PathForge's technical architecture and GPS-denied module).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes whether the published performance claims are supported by contemporaneous test data or are marketing figures, because the Complaint relies on the white paper as its principal description of PathForge's architecture and the defense will need to characterize that document accurately. If the underlying test records exist and are dated, they independently corroborate the development timeline; if they do not exist, that is a fact the defense needs to know before the document is defended as a technical statement.", "purp")

p("B.3 — MODULE-LEVEL TESTING, RELEASE AND CONTRIBUTOR EVIDENCE", "h2")

p("Q-B11.  For each module, describe the testing regime that preceded release — unit tests, integration tests, field tests, regression suites — and tell me whether those test records still exist.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 3.3 (\"extensively tested across a range of flight conditions and environments\" with benchmarks \"recorded during standardized testing at Meridian Dynamics' flight test facility and at customer deployment sites\"), Section 4.4 (GPS-denied module \"tested extensively across multiple GPS-denied environment types\") and Section 5.4 (swarm module \"tested in field conditions\"); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 118-119 (alleging substantial similarity and asserting that similarities are consistent with copying).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Test records are the most reliable contemporaneous proof that a module was independently developed and hardened over time, and they are dated in a way that marketing documents are not. They also support the white paper's characterization of PathForge as a tested production platform rather than a derivative of another codebase, which is the factual premise of the non-infringement and independent-development positions.", "purp")

p("Q-B12.  Give me the release history for the module you worked on — version numbers, release dates, and what changed in each release — and identify the release records.", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.2 timeline (September 2020: PathForge v1.0 commercial launch comprising the Navigation Module and Hardware Integration Layer; 2021-2022 continued enhancements, Swarm Coordination Module production deployment in Q1 2021, Analytics Dashboard release in Q3 2021) and Section 5.1 (first production deployment of the swarm module in early 2021); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 56 (alleging launch in or about September 2020) and para. 59 (alleging cumulative revenue in excess of $50 million since launch).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: A dated release history is the backbone of the development-timeline defense and is directly usable to test the Complaint's inference at paras. 54 and 140 that PathForge could not have been built on the asserted timeline without misappropriated material. Release records also fix the dates relevant to the '889 Patent, which was filed June 22, 2020, between the asserted swarm design start and the September 2020 launch.", "purp")

p("Q-B13.  Who else worked on your module, including anyone who has since left Meridian, and what did each of them contribute?", "q")
p("Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 1 (a dedicated engineering team of approximately 45 working full-time on PathForge development and customer integration), Section 2 (the white paper is attributed to Holt and the \"PathForge Engineering Team\") and Section 7.1 (each module \"was developed as an independent engineering effort within the broader PathForge program\"); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 7.1(a)-(b) (non-solicitation and hiring restrictions on former SkyVault employees during the twelve months following termination).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Identifies additional custodians and additional witnesses, including former employees whose departure may make their records harder to obtain and who should be interviewed or preserved early. It also builds the contributor record module by module, which is what an independent-development defense requires: not a company-level assertion, but a named person for each body of work.", "purp")

p("Q-B14.  Were you ever asked to use, review, reproduce or avoid any material from another company, including SkyVault, and describe how any such instruction was given and documented.", "q")
p("Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 4.2 (prohibition on connecting personal storage devices or transferring Company data without prior written approval), Section 3.1(b)-(c) (non-disclosure and non-use obligations) and Section 3.3(a) (permitted disclosures only to Company employees or authorized contractors with a need to know); meridian-cd-response.docx para. 11 (representation that Meridian \"respects the intellectual property rights of others\" and maintains compliance processes to guard against unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 7.2 final paragraph (independent development assertion).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests whether the compliance processes described in the April 5 Response were operating at the engineering level during the relevant period, and whether any instruction about third-party material was ever given. A documented instruction with a date is strong evidence of good-faith compliance; the absence of any instruction is itself a fact that counsel needs before the representation is relied upon in a filing.", "purp")

p("Q-B15.  Identify the people at Meridian who would have received, reviewed or responded to the March 2024 letter from SkyVault's counsel or to the April 2024 response, other than the legal department.", "q")
p("Source: meridian-cd-response.docx, addressee line (letter to Theresa N. Voss, Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP, dated April 5, 2024), first paragraph (the firm writes \"on behalf of Meridian and its officers and directors\") and cc line (Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian Dynamics, Inc.); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 61 (the March 12, 2024 letter was addressed to Priya Chandrasekaran, CEO, at Meridian's Austin headquarters) and para. 62 (the April 5, 2024 response acknowledged receipt and refused the demands).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Maps the factual receipt-and-routing chain for the notice correspondence, which is the discoverable predicate for the willfulness allegations, and identifies which non-lawyers hold responsive documents. The question is framed to elicit who received and handled the correspondence as a business matter, and should not be extended into what any lawyer advised about it.", "purp")
PYEOF

  "description": "Write memo part 3 (technical team)"
}

{
  "command": "cat > /tmp/memo/part4.py <<'PYEOF'
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# Part 4: Category C - legal lead
CONTENT = []
def p(t="", k="body"): CONTENT.append((k, t))

p("VI. CATEGORY C — MERIDIAN'S LEGAL LEAD", "h1")
p("Function in this round. The legal lead — identified in the furnished materials as Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, who is copied on the April 5, 2024 response — is the witness who can establish the discoverable chronology of Meridian's response to the March 2024 allegations, verify or correct the factual bases of the representations made in that response, and define the privilege boundary for every other interview in this round. The legal lead should not be asked engineering questions and should not be treated as a source of technical fact. The interview is deliberately divided into two tracks that must be conducted in order: Track 1 (Questions C-1 through C-12) addresses discoverable business facts and the factual predicate for Meridian's public positions; Track 2 (Questions C-13 through C-18) addresses the privilege architecture and should be conducted only after Track 1 is complete, so that factual answers are not shaped by the privilege discussion. Counsel conducting the interview should state on the record at the start of Track 2 that the discussion is for the purpose of identifying protected material and obtaining legal advice, and should document that statement.", "body")

p("C.1 — TRACK 1: DISCOVERABLE FACTS, THE RESPONSE CHRONOLOGY, AND THE PREDICATE FOR MERIDIAN'S REPRESENTATIONS", "h2")

p("Q-C1.  Describe how the March 12, 2024 letter from Callister, Voss & Greenbaum reached Meridian, who opened it, who was told about it, and what happened next.", "q")
p("Source: skyvault-complaint.docx para. 61 (letter dated March 12, 2024 sent by Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP and addressed to Priya Chandrasekaran, CEO, at Meridian's Austin headquarters, identifying the '561, '227 and '889 Patents and the trade secret and copyright claims, and demanding cessation, $15 million in licensing fees and a full forensic audit of Meridian's source code repositories); meridian-cd-response.docx, first paragraph (acknowledging receipt of the March 12, 2024 letter and stating that Brackwell & Haines writes on behalf of Meridian and its officers and directors).", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the receipt and routing chronology from the witness who handled it, which is the discoverable factual predicate for the willfulness allegations at Complaint paras. 63, 69-70, 78 and 86. The March 12, 2024 letter itself was not furnished, so nothing beyond Complaint para. 61 and the April 5 Response may be attributed to it; this question is also the mechanism for identifying and obtaining Meridian's copy. The answer should be recorded as a timeline with dates and custodians, separate from any legal assessment of the letter.", "purp")

p("Q-C2.  When was Brackwell & Haines retained, and what was the scope of the engagement as you understood it?", "q")
p("Source: meridian-cd-response.docx, letterhead and signature block (Brackwell & Haines LLP, 600 Congress Avenue, Suite 3200, Austin, Texas; Laura Brackwell, Partner) and first paragraph (\"This firm represents Meridian Dynamics, Inc. (\"Meridian\") in connection with the matters raised in your March 12, 2024 letter\").", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Fixes the retention date, which is the anchor for the privilege analysis in Track 2 and for the point at which Meridian's preservation obligations and work-product protections began. The date of retention is itself a discoverable fact even though the advice given after it is not.", "purp")

p("Q-C3.  Describe what Meridian did to preserve documents, devices, repositories and communications after the letter arrived: what was issued, when, to whom, and by what means.", "q")
p("Source: meridian-cd-response.docx paras. 10-16 (Meridian's denial of the patent, trade secret and copyright allegations; assertion of independent development; reservation of non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability and independent-development defenses; declination of the cessation, payment and audit demands) and para. 16 (reservation of rights and defenses, including challenges to patent validity); exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Rows #40 (exit interview scheduled, \"IT to preserve all logs and endpoint data per litigation hold\"), #41 (permissions audit initiated for user mholt across all Engineering subspaces), #45 (\"Forensic image of workstation SV-ENG-WS-014 requested. Hargrove Forensics Group engaged per counsel authorization\") and #49 (workstation secured in IT evidence storage; forensic imaging scheduled) as a comparator showing what a documented, contemporaneous preservation sequence looks like.", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Preservation conduct is litigated independently of the merits and is one of the few areas where a defendant can be sanctioned for conduct rather than for infringement. Establishing what was actually done, when, and by whom is therefore a priority, and the answer should be verified against the written hold notices and IT records rather than accepted from recollection. The Exhibit F entries are cited as a comparator because they show the level of documentation SkyVault itself generated in 2018 for a comparable event.", "purp")

p("Q-C4.  Since March 2024, has Meridian suspended, modified or continued any routine document-retention, deletion or device-replacement practice, and if so, describe the change and when it took effect.", "q")
p("Source: meridian-cd-response.docx para. 16 (reservation of all rights, claims and defenses, including challenges to validity, and reservation of the right to seek attorneys' fees and costs if litigation is initiated); exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Rows #41 (permissions audit initiated) and #42-#43 (ACCESS_REVOKED and VPN_ACCESS_REVOKED on 02/13/2018 per HR directive, ref INC-2018-00417) as a comparator for the type of access and retention actions a documented response includes.", "src")
p("Evidentiary purpose: Tests whether ordinary retention practices continued after notice, which is the standard preservation question and one that is entirely factual. p("VII. LEAD-FAMILY COVERAGE MATRIX", "h1")

Each is treated above as an interview-confirmation or document-collection task and must not be recorded in the interview file as an established fact.  ("Holt's SkyVault personnel file, onboarding records, badge and systems access records, performance reviews, compensation records and exit-interview record", "Q-A1, Q-A4, Q-A7; Q-C9, Q-C11"),

 ("Meridian's source code repositories, commit history, branch records, code review records and contributor attribution", "Q-A18; Q-B1, Q-B3, Q-B13"),
 ("Meridian's design documents, requirements, architecture records, notebooks and prototypes from 2018-2021", "Q-A10, Q-A15 to Q-A17; Q-B2, Q-B9"),

p("No single order is correct for every case, and the recommendation below should be revisited once the first two interviews are complete and once the initial document collections have been returned. The order that best fits the present record, the privilege posture and the available documents is as follows.", "body")

p("First: the Meridian legal lead, Track 1 only (Questions C-1 through C-12). This category should go first for three reasons. The legal lead can fix the discoverable chronology of the March-April 2024 response, which is the predicate for the willfulness allegations and the earliest-litigated preservation issues, and that chronology does not depend on any technical witness. The legal lead can also identify, before any other interview is scheduled, which Meridian personnel hold responsive documents and which have already been asked to prepare factual accounts — information that determines who else must be interviewed and in what order. Finally, Track 1 lets counsel map the privilege boundary from the inside before speaking to witnesses whose recollections could otherwise be shaped by an incomplete understanding of what is protected. Track 2 (Questions C-13 through C-18) should be completed with the same witness once Track 1 is documented, and before any technical interview is conducted.", "body")

p("Second: Dr. Holt (Questions A-1 through A-32), after the conflicts check described at Q-A7 has been completed. Holt should be second because he is the only witness who can provide the connecting account across all six lead families, and because his interview produces the specific document requests — repositories, design records, the F:\\SkyVault_Export\\ destination and the SanDisk device identifier from Exhibit F, and the white paper drafting file — that the technical interviews and the collections will then be organized around. p("Third and subsequently: the Meridian technical team, module by module (Questions B-1 through B-15), beginning with the witness who worked on the module most directly implicated by the Complaint's claim charts. By that point counsel will have the legal lead's document map, Holt's account, and the first returned collections, so each engineer can be asked to confirm or contradict a specific proposition rather than to reconstruct history from memory. The order within this category should follow the modules: multi-sensor fusion first, because the Complaint's '561 Patent claim chart is the most developed and the white paper's Section 3 is the most detailed; GPS-denied navigation and adaptive path optimization second, because that is where the DroneNav provenance question and the '227 Patent overlap; and swarm coordination third, because the white paper itself dates that module to 2019 with production deployment in 2021 and the '889 Patent was filed June 22, 2020, making its chronology the most easily tested against release records.", "body")

p("How this sequence tests later accounts. Sequencing the interviews this way turns each later interview into a verification step against an already-documented record. The legal lead's chronology is tested against Holt's recollection of the same events and against the written hold and routing records, so any divergence is visible immediately rather than at a deposition. Holt's account of what he took, retained and used (Q-A6, Q-A7, Q-A21, Q-A32) is tested against Exhibit F's row-level event data, against the SanDisk device identifier and the F:\\SkyVault_Export\\ destination path, and against the technical witnesses' systems-level answer at Q-B5. Holt's account of the PathForge starting point and timeline (Q-A10, Q-A15 to Q-A18) is tested against repository commit metadata, release records and the engineers' own module histories at Q-B1, Q-B2 and Q-B12 — records that were created contemporaneously and that do not depend on anyone's memory. The white paper's provenance claims (Q-A22 to Q-A28) are tested against the engineers' source-by-source answers at Q-B6 through Q-B9 and against the dependency and license records, which will show whether the four published references reflect actual use or only citation. And the independent-development and compliance representations in the April 5 Response (Q-C5, Q-C6) are tested last, against everything collected, so that Meridian knows before it repeats those representations in a filing whether they are supported, need qualification, or need to be withdrawn.", "body")
p("Two practical cautions apply to the sequence. First, if the legal lead's Track 1 answers show that preservation steps were incomplete or that responsive records have been lost, that issue should be addressed with counsel before any further interviews, because it changes the risk profile of every subsequent session. Second, if the technical interviews produce an account that differs materially from Holt's, counsel should not attempt to reconcile the two in the same session; the divergence should be documented and the affected questions re-asked after the records are collected.", "body")

p("X. IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS", "h1")
p("1.  Complete a conflicts assessment covering Dr. Holt's dual status as a Meridian witness and a party to the ECIAA before scheduling his interview, and before the Q-A7 line of questioning on return and destruction obligations.", "body")
p("2.  Issue or confirm a written litigation hold covering the custodians and systems identified at Q-C3, Q-C9 and Q-C11, and collect the written hold notices and the preservation records.", "body")
p("3.  Collect, in parallel with the interviews rather than after them, the highest-value records: Meridian repository and commit metadata (Q-B3), design and test records for the three modules (Q-B2, Q-B9, Q-B10, Q-B11), release records (Q-B12), dependency and license inventory (Q-B8), Meridian's copy of the March 12, 2024 letter (Q-C1), and any internal assessment prepared after March 2024 (Q-C12).", "body")
p("4.  Preserve and, if it still exists, secure the SanDisk device identified in Exhibit F Row #34 and any successor media, and document chain of custody; this is the one physical item in the furnished record whose whereabouts are unknown and whose status materially affects both the breach-of-contract theory and any remediation proposal.", "body")
p("5.  Prepare, from the module-by-module repository map developed at Q-B3, a proportionate source-code production proposal to be offered under a protective order, so that Meridian's position on code production is affirmative rather than the blanket refusal recorded at April 5 Response para. 15.", "body")
p("6.  Do not repeat the independent-development or compliance representations from the April 5 Response in any filing or deposition until the verification tasks at Q-C5, Q-C6, Q-B8 and Q-B14 have been completed.", "body")

p("— End of memorandum —", "end")
p("Privileged and confidential. Attorney work product prepared in anticipation of litigation. Do not distribute, quote, or produce.", "end")

             after=None, left=None, color=None, font="Calibri", keep=False):

        r.bold = bold; r.italic = italic
        r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.name = font
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = color
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    if before is not None: pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if after is not None: pf.space_after = Pt(after)
    if left is not None: pf.left_indent = Inches(left)
    if keep: pf.keep_with_next = True
    return p

def add_heading(text, level):
    cfg = {1: (12.5, True, RGBColor(0x14,0x2A,0x4C), 14, 5),
           2: (10.8, True, RGBColor(0x1F,0x3E,0x6B), 11, 4),
           3: (10, True,  RGBColor(0x1F,0x3E,0x6B), 9, 3)}[level]
    size, bold, col, before, after = cfg
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    r = p.add_run(text); r.bold = bold; r.font.size = Pt(size)
    r.font.name = "Calibri"; r.font.color.rgb = col
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(before); pf.space_after = Pt(after)
    pf.keep_with_next = True
    return p

def render(kind, text):
    if kind == "banner":
        add_para(text, size=9, bold=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER,
                 after=10, color=RGBColor(0x8B,0x1A,0x1A))
    elif kind == "title":
        add_para(text, size=16, bold=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER,
                 before=2, after=4, color=RGBColor(0x14,0x2A,0x4C))
    elif kind == "subtitle":
        add_para(text, size=10.5, italic=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, after=2)
    elif kind == "subtitle2":
        add_para(text, size=9.5, italic=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, after=12)
    elif kind == "meta":
        add_para(text, size=9.5, after=1, left=0.1)
    elif kind == "h1":
        add_heading(text, 1)
    elif kind == "h2":
        add_heading(text, 2)
    elif kind == "h3":
        add_heading(text, 3)
    elif kind == "body":
        add_para(text, size=10, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY, after=6)
    elif kind == "q":
        add_para(text, size=10, bold=True, left=0.18, before=6, after=2)
    elif kind == "src":
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        r = p.add_run("Source: "); r.bold = True; r.italic = True
        r.font.size = Pt(9); r.font.name = "Calibri"
        r2 = p.add_run(text.replace("Source: ", "", 1))
        r2.font.size = Pt(9); r2.italic = True; r2.font.name = "Calibri"
        pf = p.paragraph_format
        pf.left_indent = Inches(0.36); pf.space_after = Pt(2)
        pf.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    elif kind == "purp":
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        r = p.add_run("Evidentiary purpose: "); r.bold = True; r.italic = True
        r.font.size = Pt(9); r.font.name = "Calibri"
        r2 = p.add_run(text.replace("Evidentiary purpose: ", "", 1))
        r2.font.size = Pt(9); r2.italic = True; r2.font.name = "Calibri"
        pf = p.paragraph_format
        pf.left_indent = Inches(0.36); pf.space_after = Pt(5)
        pf.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    elif kind == "end":
        add_para(text, size=9.5, italic=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, before=6, after=2)

def add_table(rows, widths, header_bg="1F3E6B", first_col_bold=False):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=len(rows[0]))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            cells[ci].text = ""
            para = cells[ci].paragraphs[0]
            r = para.add_run(val)
            r.font.size = Pt(8.5); r.font.name = "Calibri"
            if ri == 0:
                r.bold = True; r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF)
                set_cell_bg(cells[ci], header_bg)
            else:
                if first_col_bold and ci == 0:
                    r.bold = True
                if ri % 2 == 0:
                    set_cell_bg(cells[ci], "F2F5FA")
            para.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            para.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
    for row in t.rows:
        for ci, w in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[ci].width = Inches(w)
    return t

  - **Dr. Marcus Holt** — 32 questions across all six lead families
