rubric.criterion: The Holt section locates the ECIAA disclosure of the RoboNav sensor-calibration tool.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分的 Q-A12 明确定位至 `holt-eciaa-agreement.docx` 的 Exhibit A Prior Inventions table 第 2 行，并注明其中披露的 “RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit (open-source)”、2015 年、GitHub 地址及 MIT License。

rubric.criterion: The Holt prior-work questions ask for content, origin, contributors, pre-SkyVault records, and relationship to PathForge without presuming overlap.
rubric.reason: Q-A11至Q-A14涵盖既有工作的内容、形成时间/来源、SkyVault任职前记录及与PathForge的关系，且以开放式方式询问、未预设重合；但未实际询问这些既有工作的共同开发者或其他贡献者。Q-A12仅问“who else used it”，不等同于询问contributors，因此未完整满足该标准。

rubric.criterion: The PathForge development questions locate the whitepaper's stated development-start timing.
rubric.reason: 备忘录在 PathForge 开发问题中明确定位白皮书的开发起点表述，例如引用 Section 1 的“Developed from the ground up beginning in 2018”及 Section 7.2 的“April 2018…PathForge development begins”，并进一步按模块引用 Q3 2018、Q1 2019、Q2 2019 等起始时间进行询问。

rubric.criterion: The PathForge development-start questions seek early requirements, repositories, architecture materials, testing records, and personnel.
rubric.reason: 备忘录的 PathForge 开发起点问题覆盖了所列事项：Q-A10、Q-B2询问最早工作成果和前身；Q-A18、Q-B3询问代码库、分支、文件路径及初始提交；Q-B4及Q-A15至Q-A17询问各模块架构；Q-A19、Q-B10至Q-B12询问测试与发布记录；Q-B1、Q-B13询问参与人员、入职时间和具体贡献。

rubric.criterion: The Meridian technical-team section locates the whitepaper's DroneNav public-project reference.
rubric.reason: Meridian technical-team section expressly locates the DroneNav reference. Q-B6 cites the whitepaper’s References list and Sections 2, 4.2, and 7.2; Q-B7 further cites Sections 2, 4.2, and 7.2, including DroneNav’s first-commit date and public GitHub-project details.

rubric.criterion: The Holt section locates the whitepaper authorship and title information for Holt.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分设有“A.4 — THE WHITE PAPER'S TITLE AND AUTHORSHIP INFORMATION”，并在 Q-A22 明确定位白皮书标题“PathForge: Next-Generation Autonomous Navigation”、日期及封面作者信息“Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder”和“PathForge Engineering Team”。

rubric.criterion: The answer treats the whitepaper authorship and title information only as a lead for role, drafting, review, approval, or technical-information-supply questions.
rubric.reason: 备忘录仅将白皮书封面的标题及“Dr. Marcus Holt / PathForge Engineering Team”署名作为访谈线索。Q-A22询问文件如何形成、各节由谁起草及Holt的角色，Q-A23询问发布前审查与批准，Q-A24至Q-A25询问独立开发表述及技术资料来源，并未仅凭署名认定实际作者身份或技术贡献。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section locates the counsel response made on behalf of Meridian and its officers and directors to SkyVault's demand letter.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分明确定位至 meridian-cd-response.docx 的首段，指出 Brackwell & Haines 就 SkyVault 2024年3月12日来函所涉事项代表“Meridian and its officers and directors”作出2024年4月5日回函；C-1、C-2等问题均据此设计。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead questions use the counsel response to probe receipt, escalation, investigation, response authority, and materials reviewed.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分以2024年4月5日律师回函为线索，明确询问了来函的接收与内部流转（Q-C1）、获知及升级处理人员（Q-C1、Q-C11）、内部调查或技术评估（Q-C5、Q-C12）、对外回应权限（Q-C8），以及回函前审阅和支撑相关陈述的材料（Q-C5、Q-C9、Q-C12）。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section locates the response's visible cc line identifying Jordan Kessler as Meridian VP of Legal.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分明确引用 `meridian-cd-response.docx` 的可见抄送栏，并写明“cc line (Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian Dynamics, Inc., via email)”。

rubric.criterion: The Jordan Kessler questions seek his role in receiving, reviewing, approving, or coordinating the response without assuming final authority.
rubric.reason: 法律负责人部分未预设 Jordan Kessler 拥有最终决定权，并通过 Q-C1 询问来函的接收与内部流转、Q-C2 询问外部律师聘任、Q-C5 至 Q-C8 询问回函陈述的事实审查基础、拒绝审计的形成及沟通协调，另以 Q-C11 至 Q-C12 追问其他参与者和内部审查，足以查明其接收、审阅、批准或协调回函过程中的实际角色。

rubric.criterion: The response uses open-ended wording for matters that can only be confirmed through interviews.
rubric.reason: 对需证人确认的事项普遍采用开放式问法，如“please describe”“walk me through”“tell me how”等，要求证人自行陈述任职、访问、开发来源、文件流转及诉前响应事实，而非将缺失材料或争议事实预设为真。

rubric.criterion: The response identifies missing records as interview-confirmation or document-request topics rather than confirmed facts.
rubric.reason: 产出明确将未提供的材料列为开放事项，并反复转化为证人确认或文件调取任务，而非既定事实。例如第二节写明“Not furnished ... and therefore treated as open”，第八节又说明每类缺失材料“is treated ... as an interview-confirmation or document-collection task and must not be recorded ... as an established fact”，并在问题中要求识别、调取人员档案、代码库、开发/测试/发布记录、保全记录、内部沟通、合规材料、完整取证数据及技术比对。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum provides questions that can actually be asked orally of the designated witnesses, rather than only topic headings, document lists or statements of desired findings.
rubric.reason: 备忘录为三类指定证人提供了大量可直接口头询问的完整问题，例如要求 Holt “Starting with your arrival at SkyVault, please describe...”以及询问技术团队“Identify the repositories, branches and file paths...”。内容并非仅有主题标题、文件清单或预期结论。

rubric.criterion: The memo stays within the provided source universe and uses missing documents only as confirmation or production topics.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确将事实来源限定为五份指定材料，并逐一说明其证明范围。未提供的人员档案、代码库、开发与测试记录、保全材料、内部通信、完整取证数据、技术比对及2024年3月12日来函等，均被列为待访谈确认、调取、收集或核验事项，而未被表述为既定事实；对该来函的内容也明确仅依据诉状第61段和4月5日回函。

rubric.criterion: The memo assigns witness topics to the witness category best positioned to answer them.
rubric.reason: 备忘录按知识范围合理分工：Holt 负责其任职、访问、既有工作及个人行为；技术团队负责模块开发、代码库、依赖、测试和发布记录；法务负责人负责诉前回函、保全及特权边界。文中还明确法务负责人“should not be asked engineering questions”，并以跨证人核验补充而非混淆职责。

rubric.criterion: The memo does not upgrade a limited interview-preparation record into a full infringement, provenance, preservation, or merits conclusion.
rubric.reason: 备忘录始终将材料限定为访谈线索和待核实立场：明确说明诉状仅是原告主张、回函及白皮书中的独立开发/合规表述属于未经宣誓的当事方立场、Exhibit F 只是选定事件摘录，并反复要求通过代码库、提交记录、测试、发布及保全记录核验。其亦明确声明不构成侵权比对、实体胜诉意见或完整保全结论，未将现有有限记录升级为最终侵权、技术来源、保全或实体结论。

rubric.criterion: The answer states an evidence gap or unconfirmed point as a definite conclusion.
rubric.reason: 备忘录虽总体谨慎，但将未经材料确认的证人知识范围写成定论。例如称 Holt 是“the single witness whose knowledge spans every lead family”及“the only witness who can connect”2018 年事件与后续开发；五份材料只能显示其角色和关联，不能证明其实际知识范围或其为唯一知情人。

rubric.criterion: No non-empty, readable Microsoft Word (.docx) memorandum containing substantive, scorable text is submitted, including where the required file is missing, empty, corrupted, in the wrong file format, or wholly unreadable.
rubric.reason: modelResponse 明确提交了“Artifact: result.docx”，且展示了大量可读、实质性的英文访谈设计备忘录正文；不存在文件缺失、空白、格式错误、损坏或全文不可读的情形。

rubric.criterion: The response is severely redundant, repeatedly restating the same facts, questions, sources, purposes, or cautions without adding a distinct interview function, thereby materially impairing the memorandum’s concision and usability.
rubric.reason: 备忘录存在严重重复并明显影响可用性：例如 Exhibit F 的六次导出、4,700 个文件、SanDisk 设备和目标路径在 A6、A21、B5、结尾顺序说明及后续步骤中反复详述；独立开发与合规声明及其“未经验证的当事方立场”在来源综述、Holt、技术组、法务组和结尾多次重述；材料证明范围、缺失材料、特权边界和访谈顺序也分别在前言、各节 conduct note、矩阵、开放事项及 next steps 中重复。大量问题（如 A18/B3、A19/B8/B14/C5-C6、A26/B6-B7）询问高度重合的代码来源、依赖、合规和开发记录，篇幅远超实现不同访谈功能所需，实质削弱了简洁性和现场使用效率。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum identifies Exhibit F as a 50-event selected extract from a stated 12,847-event review population for account mholt and limits it to SkyVault-side access, export, device, and response leads rather than treating it as a complete forensic record or proof of Meridian receipt or PathForge use.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确称 Exhibit F 是针对账户“mholt”的 SkyVault 侧选定摘录，完整审计日志有 12,847 个事件，其中仅选取 50 个，并强调其“是经过筛选的子集，而非完整记录”。同时明确指出该材料不证明文件进入 Meridian 系统或被 PathForge 使用，仅将其用于访问、导出、USB 设备及后续响应等调查线索。

rubric.criterion: The Holt interview reconciles the bulk removable-media event's 2018-02-09 02:18 UTC timestamp with its displayed February 8, 8:18 p.m. Central local time, or otherwise uses the timestamp without creating a false chronology.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分明确核对了该事件的时区日期差异。Q-A6 的 Source 引用 Exhibit F Row #34 的 2018-02-09 02:18:12 UTC / 2018-02-08 08:18:12 PM CT；Evidentiary purpose 进一步指出 Event Date 为 02/09、CT 列为 02/08，并要求访谈确认其记忆中的实际日历日期，未制造错误时间线。

rubric.criterion: Across its questions and annotations, the memorandum independently distinguishes pleaded allegations, the final counsel response's advocacy statements, the public White Paper's later marketing/technical assertions, operative ECIAA terms and disclosures, and logged forensic events, and does not use one source type as automatic proof of a different proposition.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确且反复区分五类来源的证明范围：称诉状内容为 SkyVault 的 allegations；称 2024-04-05 回函中的独立开发、否认和合规陈述为“party advocacy”“unsworn litigation positions”；将白皮书限定为 2022 年公开营销/技术陈述而非开发记录；将 ECIAA 作为合同条款及 Exhibit A 既有发明披露；将 Exhibit F 限定为 mholt 账户的精选事件摘录而非不当行为或使用证明。各问题的 Source 与 Evidentiary purpose 也通常分别说明材料支持的命题，并多次强调导出/访问不等于保留、使用、复制或误用，未将一种来源自动升级为另一事实命题的证明。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum recognizes that the complaint lists patents, a copyright registration, the ECIAA, Exhibit F and the White Paper, while the supplied universe does not include the patents, registration, full March 12 letter, source code, or a technical comparison, and therefore treats those missing materials as collection or confirmation needs rather than silently supplying their contents.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确区分了诉状所列的三项专利、版权登记、ECIAA、Exhibit F 和白皮书，并指出题包未提供专利文本、版权登记材料、3月12日完整来函、源代码及技术比对。其将这些内容列为开放的调取或证人确认事项，如要求取得来函副本、代码库、版权登记交存材料及开展技术比较，而未擅自补充其内容。

rubric.criterion: The Holt section connects the February 15 exit-interview/device note to ECIAA return, deletion, certification, and exit obligations, while asking Holt to confirm what occurred and avoiding treatment of the SkyVault administrator note as conclusive proof of breach.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分的 Q-A7 明确引用 Exhibit F Row #46 的 2028? exit-interview/device 管理员记录，并关联 ECIAA Sections 3.5(a)-(c) 的返还、永久删除及书面认证义务和 Section 4.4 的离职程序义务。问题以“Tell me what happened...”要求 Holt 说明实际经过、设备及副本去向和是否曾作删除认证，同时提示不得要求其作法律定性，未将 SkyVault 的管理员记录直接视为违约的决定性证明。

rubric.criterion: The Holt section addresses the January 24 view and/or February 8 bulk export from the Business/CustomerData space and seeks purpose, authorization, content and corroboration, using the log's 'outside normal Engineering scope' note as a lead rather than a legal conclusion.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分的 Q-A21 明确引用 Exhibit F Row #17（1月24日查看 customer_contracts_summary_2017.xlsx）和 Row #32（2月8日从 /Business/CustomerData/ 导出84个文件），询问文件内容、访问/导出目的及其是否进入 Meridian 系统；Q-A4至Q-A6进一步询问访问如何获准、适用限制及后续副本去向，以便通过系统、设备和相关人员记录交叉核验。备忘录将“outside normal Engineering scope”仅作为需调查的日志标记和线索，并未据此认定越权或违法。

rubric.criterion: The Holt questions distinguish the ECIAA's Confidential Information definition and invention-assignment provisions from its general-skills/public-information allowance and Exhibit A prior-invention disclosure, and seek records capable of applying those boundaries to later PathForge work.
rubric.reason: Holt 问题明确区分了 ECIAA 的保密信息定义与发明披露/转让义务（如 Q-A1、Q-A2）以及 Section 3.4 的一般技能和公开信息许可、Section 2.1 的排除项、Section 5.3 与 Exhibit A 的既有发明披露（Q-A11 至 Q-A14）。问题还要求取得博士论文、既有代码和笔记、GitHub/MIT 许可记录、PathForge 仓库与提交历史、设计及测试记录等，以便将这些合同边界实际应用于后续 PathForge 工作。

rubric.criterion: The prior-work inquiry seeks contemporaneous substantiation for the disclosed Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm and RoboNav toolkit—such as dissertation, repository, contributor, release-date and license records—and does not confuse RoboNav with the White Paper's separate DroneNav reference.
rubric.reason: 备忘录对两项既有工作均要求同期材料佐证：Q-A11要求查找路径规划算法的论文、代码和笔记；Q-A12明确追问RoboNav的GitHub仓库、MIT许可证、使用者及是否进入PathForge，Q-A13至Q-A14还追问其他出版物、仓库及书面记录。另在Q-A25至Q-A28、Q-B6至Q-B8中将DroneNav作为白皮书引用的独立公开项目，分别核查知悉、克隆、依赖、修改和使用情况，未与RoboNav混淆。

rubric.criterion: The technical-team questions seek a module-specific provenance chain for sensor fusion, GPS-denied navigation and swarm coordination, connecting contributors and source-code/repository history, including dependencies or their non-use, to both testing and release records and the records or custodians needed to verify those links. Shared questions expressly applied to each component, including a combined Navigation Module with distinguishable sensor-fusion and GPS-denied work, qualify; questions about record absence or dependency non-use are valid, without supplying invented record contents.
rubric.reason: 技术团队部分形成了符合标准的模块级来源链。Q-B1至Q-B4要求按组件说明开发起点、前身、架构、代码复用、仓库/分支/文件路径及初始提交者；Q-B6至Q-B9逐一追问DroneNav等依赖的了解、引用、评估、克隆、导入、修改、使用或未使用；Q-B10至Q-B12要求对应的测试数据、测试记录、版本号、发布日期及发布记录；Q-B13进一步识别各模块贡献者和离职保管人。问题明确覆盖传感器融合、GPS-denied navigation和swarm coordination，并要求以提交元数据、依赖与许可证记录、测试及发布记录交叉验证，未虚构缺失记录的内容。

rubric.criterion: The technical-team questions seek underlying test plans, raw results, approvals, drafts or source records for material White Paper performance and independent-development statements instead of treating the published figures or marketing conclusion as contemporaneous provenance proof.
rubric.reason: 技术团队问题明确要求核查白皮书陈述的底层记录，而非将营销结论视为既定事实。例如 Q-B10 逐项追问性能数字所依据的测试记录，Q-B11 要求测试计划与结果，Q-B3、Q-B9、Q-B12 分别要求仓库/提交记录、改进工作的作者与日期记录、发布记录，以验证独立开发及性能陈述。

rubric.criterion: The public-source questions separately investigate DroneNav and the cited academic works by Vasquez, Nakamura and Okonkwo, and Ferreira, seeking corroborating records that distinguish awareness, citation and evaluation from modification, use or non-use. The inquiry also distinguishes cloning and dependency introduction for software sources, while academic influences can be traced through design decisions and citations; naming sources alone is insufficient.
rubric.reason: 问题分别调查了 DroneNav 与 Vasquez、Nakamura and Okonkwo、Ferreira 等学术来源。Q-B6 明确逐项区分“read, cited, evaluated, cloned, imported as a dependency, modified, used, or did not use”；Q-A26/Q-B7 单独追问 DroneNav 的克隆、下载、分叉、依赖引入及现存代码，并要求以提交历史、许可证、构建脚本等佐证；Q-A25、Q-A27、Q-A28及Q-B9则通过阅读时间、引用记录、设计选择、具体改进及设计文档等追踪学术影响，超出了仅列举来源。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section tests the non-privileged factual basis for the response's denials, independent-development assertion and compliance-process assertion, identifies records or custodians reviewed and gaps, and does not treat the sent response as proof that those assertions are true.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分明确检验回函陈述的非特权事实基础：Q-C5询问独立开发表述发送前做过何种事实核查，Q-C6核查2018—2021年及当前合规流程，Q-C9、Q-C11、Q-C12识别相关记录、系统、保管人及内部技术/事实审查。备忘录还明确将回函定性为“party advocacy”“unsworn litigation positions, not verified facts”，并要求在记录核验前不得再次依赖独立开发或合规表述，未将已发送回函视为真实性证明。

rubric.criterion: The pre-suit-response questions limit statements about the unprovided March 12 letter to what Complaint paragraph 61 and the April 5 response actually record, while separately investigating receipt, escalation, response scope, authority and transmission.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确声明未提供3月12日来函，且“不得归因超出 Complaint para. 61 和 April 5 Response 所记载内容”。Q-A29、Q-C1分别调查来函的接收、内部传递与升级；Q-C5至Q-C8调查回函事实基础、回应范围、拒绝审计的原因及对外沟通授权；Q-B15和Q-C1还追查收件、审阅、响应及传送链条，符合该标准。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section asks for Meridian's actual 2024 preservation dates, custodians, systems, actions and non-privileged completion records, and does not confuse those facts with the 2018 SkyVault-side litigation-hold, imaging and access-revocation entries in Exhibit F or assume preservation was complete.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分的 Q-C3、Q-C4、Q-C10 明确询问 2024 年实际保全措施的时间、对象、系统、执行方式及书面 hold notices、IT 记录等非特权完成记录，并要求以记录核实而非假定完整。文中将 Exhibit F 的 2018 年 SkyVault 保全、镜像和访问撤销事件反复明确标为“comparator”，未将其误作 Meridian 的保全事实。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead questions seek discoverable facts, dates, actors, custodians, actions and pre-existing business records while expressly reserving legal advice, attorney communications, strategy and mental impressions for privilege/work-product review and proposing a workable screening boundary.
rubric.reason: 法律负责人部分明确划分两个顺序执行的轨道：C1-C12询问可发现的收件时间、参与者、保全行动、文件位置、保管人及既有业务记录；C13-C18另行识别为取得法律意见而作的沟通、诉讼预期材料、律师工作成果和思维成果。备忘录还要求先完成事实轨道、再讨论特权，并通过按日期、发件人、收件人、主题及业务/法律目的分类，提出了可操作的特权筛查边界。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum converts identified proof gaps into targeted collection requests that name relevant systems, record types, custodians, date ranges or modules and explain how each target will test access, provenance, public-source use, preservation or the response chain; a generic request for all documents is insufficient.
rubric.reason: 备忘录将证明缺口具体转化为定向访谈和调取任务，而非笼统要求“全部文件”。例如要求按模块收集 Meridian 的 repository、branch、file path、initial commit、贡献者、依赖与许可证、2018–2021 年设计/测试/发布记录；按保管人和系统收集诉讼保全通知、IT 日志及 2024 年来函流转记录；并以 SanDisk 设备标识、F:\SkyVault_Export\ 路径及 Exhibit F 行号追查访问与留存。各项均说明用于检验访问范围、PathForge 来源、DroneNav 等公开来源的实际使用、保全措施或诉前回函链。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum ends with a brief recommendation identifying first, second and last witness categories and explaining why that order is workable in light of privilege scope, available records, witness knowledge and the value of using earlier interviews or collection to test later accounts. A professionally supported legal-first, technical-first, Holt-first or staged hybrid order qualifies without matching a prescribed sequence.
rubric.reason: 备忘录在第 IX 节明确建议第一访谈 Meridian legal lead、第二访谈 Dr. Holt、最后按模块访谈 technical team，并结合特权边界、文件与保全记录、各证人的知识范围及用早期访谈和调取结果交叉检验后续说法的价值，说明了该顺序的可执行理由。

rubric.criterion: The proposed sequence and actual questions form a coherent cross-witness verification plan: a record, custodian or factual account sought from an earlier witness category is used in planned later questioning to confirm, challenge, explain or refine another category’s account, while preserving what each source can and cannot establish. One connected chain or conditional follow-up plan qualifies; repeated topics without a downstream testing relationship do not.
rubric.reason: 备忘录形成了明确的跨证人核验链：先由法务负责人确定2024年来函、保全措施、记录位置及保管人，再以该时间线询问Holt，最后结合前两轮调取的材料逐模块询问技术团队。第IX节还具体说明用Exhibit F的事件、设备标识和路径核验Holt关于文件处理的回答，用代码提交、发布和测试记录及技术人员回答核验Holt的PathForge开发叙述，并明确若技术人员说法与Holt重大不一致，应记录分歧、调取记录后重新询问。全文同时持续限定诉状、回函、白皮书和Exhibit F各自能证明的范围。

rubric.criterion: Every question has Source: and Evidentiary purpose: annotations identifying the supplied filename and an available useful locator, relating the cited material to the factual premise being investigated, and explaining what the answer would establish, test or resolve. For a question relying on multiple materials, each source’s contribution is identifiable from the question and annotations rather than a collective list of filenames; one annotation block can cover coherent related follow-ups with an unambiguous mapping.
rubric.reason: 所有编号问题（A、B、C三类）后均附有“Source:”和“Evidentiary purpose:”段落；来源注明五份题包文件之一，并普遍提供段落、合同条款、工作表/Row #、日期、章节或具体文件名等有效定位。各目的段说明答案将建立、检验或解决的事项；涉及多份材料时，也通常分别说明诉状主张、合同义务、日志事件、白皮书陈述或回函立场各自支持的命题，而非仅罗列文件名。复合追问均处于同一编号及连贯主题下，映射清楚。

rubric.criterion: The Holt and/or technical-team questions test SkyVault’s allegation that materials implicated in the approximately 4,700-file USB event later reached Meridian, were disclosed to its personnel, or were used in PathForge, by seeking the custody/disposition account, any recipients or receiving systems, the component or activity involved in any claimed use, and witnesses or records capable of corroborating receipt/use or non-receipt/non-use. The inquiry treats this connection as disputed rather than established by the SkyVault-side log; contemporaneous development records and searches for SkyVault-origin artifacts are valid ways to test it.
rubric.reason: 问题充分检验了该争议连接：Q-A6、Q-A7追问约4,700个文件及USB设备的去向、后续副本和删除/返还情况；Q-A21询问SkyVault来源文件是否进入任何Meridian系统、设备或账户；Q-A32要求Holt具体说明取走、使用及未使用的材料；Q-B5从技术人员角度逐人核查Meridian仓库、文件共享、设备和账户中是否存在SkyVault来源材料，并要求配合系统与记录搜索。备忘录明确指出Exhibit F只证明导出/转移事件，不证明文件后来被Meridian接收、披露或用于PathForge，并以设备标识、目标路径、仓库提交记录、开发记录及技术人员证言作为交叉验证手段。

rubric.criterion: Substantive authored memorandum text, such as role descriptions, interview questions, source/purpose explanations or the closing recommendation, is written in a language other than English; isolated proper names, filenames, source identifiers, ordinary legal terms or short original-language source quotations within English prose are outside this error.
rubric.reason: 备忘录的角色说明、访谈问题、来源与证明目的注释、结尾建议等实质内容均使用英文；文件名、专有名称和标识符不构成该错误。

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT — PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION

WITNESS-INTERVIEW OUTLINE AND PREPARATION MEMORANDUM

SkyVault Technologies LLC v. Meridian Dynamics, Inc., Case No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG (E.D. Tex.)

Internal Fact Investigation Conducted Under Privilege at the Direction of Counsel for Meridian Dynamics, Inc.

TO:      File / Engagement Team (Meridian Dynamics, Inc.)

FROM:    Counsel for Defendant Meridian Dynamics, Inc.

DATE:    September 2026

RE:      Interview design — Dr. Marcus Holt; Meridian technical team; Meridian legal lead

STATUS:  Privileged draft. Not for production or distribution outside the defense team.

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THIS MEMORANDUM

This memorandum is an interview-design document. It states, for each of three witness categories, the function that category serves in the current round of privileged fact interviews and lists the questions that counsel can actually ask out loud. It is a planning instrument only: it is not testimony, not a declaration, not a pleading, not a claim chart, not an invalidity or non-infringement analysis, not a settlement communication, and not a merits opinion on any claim or defense. Nothing in it should be quoted, filed, or produced.

This round of interviews is being conducted before any deposition, before any written discovery responses have been served, and before any deposition-preparation session. The objective is triage: to determine, witness by witness, what Meridian personnel actually did, what they actually knew and when, what documentary records exist and where they reside, and which of the Plaintiff's allegations are factually testable rather than merely pleaded. The interviews are also designed to surface the facts that will frame the privilege boundary — which communications are discoverable business facts and which are protected attorney-client communications or attorney work product — before that boundary is tested by an adversary.

Factual statements in this memorandum are drawn exclusively from the five materials furnished for this exercise, identified below. Where a proposition rests on a party's assertion rather than on verified fact, it is labeled as such. Where a material would ordinarily exist but was not furnished, the gap is treated in the outline as an interview-confirmation or document-collection task, not as an established fact.

II. THE FIVE SOURCE MATERIALS AND WHAT EACH ACTUALLY PROVES

The interview outline that follows cites only the five materials listed below. Each is identified with a short form used throughout the outline.

1.  skyvault-complaint.docx — Plaintiff's Original Complaint ("the Complaint"). Filed October 2, 2024 in the Eastern District of Texas; Civil Action No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG; jury demand; signed by Theresa N. Voss of Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP. Asserted Counts I-IX: infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 10,234,561 (the '561 Patent), 10,891,227 (the '227 Patent) and 11,402,889 (the '889 Patent); DTSA and TUTSA trade secret misappropriation; copyright infringement of the AeroCore Firmware Suite; breach of the ECIAA; unjust enrichment; and Texas common-law unfair competition. Probative scope: this document proves what SkyVault has alleged and the relief it demands. It does not prove that any allegation is true, that any Meridian product infringes, that any trade secret was misappropriated, that any code was copied, or that any Meridian technology was derived from SkyVault. Its internal qualifiers ("On information and belief" at paras. 2, 10, 12, 49, 54, 55, 59, 60, 69, 77, 78, 86, 94, 95, 119, 120, 130 and 146) and its reservations of rights ("SkyVault reserves the right to assert additional claims ... as discovery proceeds," paras. 68, 77, 84) should be captured verbatim in the interview file, because they are useful admissions that the Plaintiff's technical case was pleaded without inspection of Meridian's code.

2.  exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx — Exhibit F, "SkyVault Technologies LLC — Confluence Workspace IT Forensic Log Extract," prepared by Hargrove Forensics Group, report dated March 5, 2018 ("Exhibit F"). Probative scope: Exhibit F is a SkyVault-side extract of selected events for the single user account 'mholt' for the review period January 1, 2018 through February 28, 2018. The "Report Metadata" sheet states that the full audit log contains 12,847 events for that period and that 50 events were selected as relevant to the engagement scope, so Exhibit F is a curated subset, not a complete record. It is a record of events attributable to a SkyVault system account, not a finding of wrongdoing, not a finding that any particular file was SkyVault property rather than a third-party or personal document, and not evidence of what happened after February 16, 2018. It also does not establish that the 4,700 files identified in Row #34 were ever opened, read, copied into any Meridian system, or used.

3.  holt-eciaa-agreement.docx — Employee Confidentiality and Invention Assignment Agreement between SkyVault Technologies LLC and Dr. Marcus Holt, effective June 13, 2016 ("the ECIAA"). Probative scope: the ECIAA is a contract. It establishes the parties' agreed obligations (Section 3 confidentiality and non-use; Section 4 systems and removable-media controls; Section 5 invention disclosure and assignment; Section 7 non-solicitation; Sections 8-9 remedies, governing law and survival) and, importantly for the defense, the contract's own exclusions and carve-outs: Section 2.1(i)-(iv) exclusions from Confidential Information (publicly available material; information known to Holt before disclosure as documented by written records; independently developed information as documented by written records; third-party disclosures); Section 3.4 preservation of general skills, knowledge and expertise and the right to use publicly available information and general industry knowledge; Section 5.3 exclusion of inventions developed entirely on the employee's own time without Company resources and the Exhibit A Prior Inventions disclosure. The ECIAA does not establish that any obligation was breached, that any particular file was confidential, or that anything Holt later built derived from SkyVault. The ECIAA contains no non-competition covenant — a point to verify against the original, since the Complaint does not plead one and a non-compete would materially change the defense posture.

4.  pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx — "PathForge: Next-Generation Autonomous Navigation," dated July 2022, attributed on its cover to "Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder" and the "PathForge Engineering Team," marked "Document Classification: Public Release / Marketing Technical Paper," and expressly an excerpt of a 42-page paper (Sections 1-5 and 7; Section 6 hardware specifications and the appendices omitted). Probative scope: the white paper is a July 2022 public technical and marketing statement. It is a statement of claimed capability and design intent as of publication. It is not a development record, not a source-code repository, not a test report, not an admission, and not evidence that any capability described was implemented in the manner or on the schedule described. Its provenance and timing assertions — "developed from the ground up beginning in 2018" (Section 1); the phased timeline in Section 7.2; "All PathForge technology was developed independently by the Meridian engineering team" (Section 7.2) — are the Defendant's own public position and must be corroborated by Meridian's internal records before they are relied on.

5.  meridian-cd-response.docx — Letter dated April 5, 2024 from Laura Brackwell of Brackwell & Haines LLP to Theresa N. Voss, responding to SkyVault's March 12, 2024 cease-and-desist letter ("the April 5 Response"). Probative scope: the April 5 Response is party advocacy. It proves that Meridian received notice of the three asserted patents and of the trade secret and copyright allegations; that Meridian denies infringement, misappropriation and copying; that Meridian asserts independent development; that Meridian declined all three demands (cessation, the $15 million licensing fee, and a source-code forensic audit); and that Meridian reserved non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability and independent-development defenses. Its statements that Meridian "independently developed its PathForge platform" and "maintains robust internal compliance processes" are unsworn litigation positions, not verified facts. The letter also reflects that Meridian's outside counsel directed that future communications be routed to Brackwell & Haines and requested that SkyVault refrain from contacting Meridian officers and employees directly.

Not furnished with this exercise, and therefore treated as open: the March 12, 2024 cease-and-desist letter itself; Exhibits A-E and G to the Complaint (the three patents, the copyright registration certificate, the ECIAA as filed, and the full white paper); Holt's SkyVault personnel file, onboarding and access records, and exit-interview record; SkyVault's or Meridian's source code repositories; Meridian development records (commit history, design documents, requirements, test and release records); Meridian's preservation and litigation-hold records; internal Meridian communications; Meridian compliance and onboarding materials; complete forensic images and full audit logs; and any technical comparison of the AeroCore firmware to the PathForge firmware. The Complaint's paragraph 61 is the only source in the furnished set for the contents of the March 12, 2024 letter. This memorandum does not attribute to that letter anything beyond what paragraph 61 of the Complaint and the April 5 Response record.

III. THREE WITNESS CATEGORIES: FUNCTION IN THIS ROUND

Category A — Dr. Marcus Holt, Meridian co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, is the only witness whose knowledge spans all six of the lead families below. He is simultaneously the former SkyVault Senior Systems Engineer named in the Complaint, the account holder identified in Exhibit F, the ECIAA signatory, the author of the Exhibit A Prior Inventions disclosure, and the named cover author of the July 2022 white paper. Section IV of this memorandum states his function in this round and sets out thirty-two questions covering his employment and access history, his disclosed prior work, the PathForge development starting point, the white paper, DroneNav and other public sources, and the pre-suit correspondence chain.

Category B — the Meridian technical team, meaning the engineering personnel who built the PathForge Navigation Module, the Swarm Coordination Module, the hardware integration layer and the analytics dashboard, plus those who can speak to repository, release and test practice, supplies what Holt cannot supply alone: a module-by-module, author-level account of how PathForge was actually built. These witnesses are the only route to the repository, dependency, test and release records that will corroborate or contradict the independent-development position asserted in the white paper and the April 5, 2024 response. Section V states their function in this round and sets out fifteen questions, including the file-level inventory needed to identify the PathForge counterparts to the three AeroCore files named in the Complaint.

Category C — Meridian's legal lead, identified in the furnished materials as Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, who is copied on the April 5, 2024 response, is not a source of engineering fact. This witness's function is to establish the discoverable chronology of Meridian's response to the March 2024 allegations, to test the factual predicate for the representations made in that response, and to define the privilege boundary for every other interview in this round. Section VI states that function and sets out eighteen questions in two ordered tracks: a factual track on discoverable events, and a privilege-design track that is conducted only afterward.

IV. CATEGORY A — DR. MARCUS HOLT (CO-FOUNDER AND CHIEF TECHNOLOGY OFFICER)

Function in this round. Holt is the single witness whose knowledge spans every lead family in this investigation: his SkyVault employment and access history, the prior work he disclosed to SkyVault in 2016, the true starting point of each PathForge module, the authorship and provenance of the July 2022 white paper, his familiarity with DroneNav and other public sources, and the pre-suit correspondence chain. His interview therefore does double duty: it must fix the factual spine — dates, credentials, system access, what he did and did not take, keep or reuse, and when each module actually began — and it must produce the list of documents that will corroborate or contradict each answer, because his account will not be accepted at face value by the Plaintiff and should not be relied on internally without records. He is also the only witness who can connect the 2018 events recorded in Exhibit F to the 2018-2021 development work described in the July 2022 white paper, which makes his account the reference point against which every later interview in this round is measured.

Conduct note. Because Holt is simultaneously a fact witness for Meridian and a party to the ECIAA, counsel should treat this as a scoping interview: open-ended questions first, documents identified by name and location second, and no characterization of contested legal conclusions. Questions about Holt's own legal exposure, if any, should be reserved for a separate session after conflicts assessment is completed.

A.1 — LEAD FAMILY 1: EMPLOYMENT, ROLE, CREDENTIALS AND SYSTEM ACCESS HISTORY

Q-A1.  Starting with your arrival at SkyVault, please describe in your own words how you came to be hired there, what position you were offered, what your start date was, and what you understood your job duties to be on day one.

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Section 1.1 (position of Senior Systems Engineer, reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Rajan Mehta; duties including research, development and engineering of UAV flight control systems, sensor fusion algorithms and flight path optimization), Section 1.3 (start date June 13, 2016), and the signature block dated June 13, 2016; skyvault-complaint.docx para. 43 (alleging hire as Senior Systems Engineer on June 13, 2016).

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the baseline employment relationship from the witness rather than from the Complaint, and tests whether Holt's actual duties were as narrow or as broad as the ECIAA and the Complaint describe. This matters because the scope of his duties frames the reach of ECIAA Section 5.2 (assignment of inventions related to the Company's current or reasonably anticipated business) and the credibility of the Complaint's sweeping claim at para. 44 that he had access to all five trade secret categories.

Q-A2.  Describe the technical work you personally performed at SkyVault, including the specific subsystems, algorithms or code you contributed to, and tell me which of that work you would describe as your own independent contribution versus work that was team-developed.

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 2.3 (definition of "Inventions"), 5.1 (disclosure obligation for inventions conceived, created, developed or reduced to practice during employment) and 5.2 (assignment of Company Inventions); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 22-23 (describing the AeroCore firmware suite and its subsystems) and para. 34 (alleging AeroCore was developed by SkyVault's engineering team including during Holt's employment).

Evidentiary purpose: Identifies the specific SkyVault work to which Holt can speak from personal knowledge, and separates that from team work he can only describe secondhand. This determines the limits of his admissible testimony and helps counsel decide which Meridian technical witnesses or former SkyVault engineers are needed to cover the rest. It also begins the record on what Holt personally created, which is the first step in testing any later assertion that PathForge code derives from his SkyVault work.

Q-A3.  Describe your educational background and any prior employment or research positions you held before joining SkyVault, and identify the specific subject matter of your doctoral research.

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, recital ("Employee holds a PhD in Robotics from the Georgia Institute of Technology (2015) and possesses specialized skills in robotics, autonomous systems, and related engineering disciplines"); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A Prior Inventions table (row 1: "Autonomous Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm," 2014-2015, developed as part of PhD dissertation research at Georgia Institute of Technology, no patent filed); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 42 (alleging a 2015 Georgia Tech PhD in Robotics with doctoral research on autonomous navigation and multi-sensor data integration).

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the pre-existing knowledge base that predates SkyVault and is therefore outside the ECIAA's reach under Section 3.4 (general skills and knowledge) and Section 2.1(ii) (information known to Employee prior to disclosure, as documented by written records). The overlap between the doctoral subject matter and the accused PathForge functionality is the core of the independent-development defense, so it must be documented from the witness and then corroborated with the dissertation and any associated records.

Q-A4.  Walk me through the SkyVault systems, repositories and workspaces you could reach with your credentials, how your access was granted, and whether anyone ever restricted or narrowed that access during your employment.

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 4.1 (Company computer systems, networks, servers, email accounts and data storage systems including internal wiki and knowledge management platforms are Company property) and 4.3 (monitoring and consent to monitoring of file access and data transfers); skyvault-complaint.docx para. 44 (alleging broad access to AeroCore, sensor fusion algorithms, flight path optimization models, swarm communication protocols, LiDAR hardware integration specifications, and customer lists and pricing strategies through customer demonstrations and proposal development) and paras. 40 and 93 (alleging password-protected systems and limiting access to authorized personnel).

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the actual scope of Holt's authorized access from his own account, which is the foundation for evaluating the Complaint's access-based trade secret theory. The answer also frames whether SkyVault's access controls were as restrictive as paras. 40 and 93 assert, and whether any access restriction or permission change was ever communicated to him before February 2018.

Q-A5.  Describe how a typical engineer at SkyVault used the Confluence workspace — what was stored there, whether downloading or exporting workspace content to a local drive was routine, and whether you were ever given any instruction, training or written policy about moving workspace content off the system.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, "Forensic Log" sheet, Rows #1-#32 (FILE_VIEW, FILE_DOWNLOAD and BULK_EXPORT events by user account mholt from Confluence across /SkyVault/Engineering/SensorFusion/, /FlightPath/, /SwarmProtocol/ and /HardwareIntegration/ between 01/03/2018 and 02/08/2018, including six BULK_EXPORT events at Rows #27-#32 with destinations on Local Disk C:\Users\mholt\Downloads); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 4.1 and 4.2 (prohibiting transfer of Company data to personal devices or accounts and connection of personal storage devices without prior written approval of the supervisor or IT department).

Evidentiary purpose: Tests whether the conduct Exhibit F records was unusual or was ordinary workplace practice, and whether SkyVault ever communicated the Section 4.2 approval requirement in practice. This is directly relevant to the trade secret claim's reasonable-secrecy element and to any argument that Holt lacked fair notice of the restriction. It also identifies the SkyVault personnel (IT, HR, supervisors) who can confirm or rebut the practice testimony.

Q-A6.  Turning to the events of February 2018: describe what you did with SkyVault workspace content in the days before your last day, including any export, copy or transfer of files, and tell me what you did with any copies afterwards.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Rows #27-#32 (six BULK_EXPORT events from 02/02/2018 through 02/08/2018 totaling 1,526 files and approximately 9,681 MB to local export folders, including 84 files from /SkyVault/Business/CustomerData/ at Row #32), Row #33 (USB_DEVICE_CONNECTED on 02/09/2018 at 02:17:44 UTC / 08:17:44 PM CT on 02/08, SanDisk Ultra 128GB, device identifier USB\VID_0781&PID_5581\4C530001221029118035), Row #34 (BULK_COPY_TO_REMOVABLE on 02/09/2018 at 02:18:12 UTC / 08:18:12 PM CT on 02/08, 4,700 files, 18,473.2 MB, destination Removable Disk F:\SkyVault_Export\, flagged ALERT — bulk transfer to removable media exceeds threshold (>500 files)), and Row #35 (USB_DEVICE_DISCONNECTED at 03:42:58 UTC / 09:42:58 PM CT on 02/08).

Evidentiary purpose: Fixes the central factual event in the case from the witness rather than from SkyVault's extract. The event timestamps and the time-zone discrepancy matter: Exhibit F's own "Event Date" column records 02/09/2018 while the "Event Time (CT)" column records 08:17:44 PM on 02/08, so the interview must establish which calendar day Holt recalls and what he was doing at that hour. The destination path F:\SkyVault_Export\ and the SanDisk device serial are the two identifiers that will be used to test any later claim about where the files went.

Q-A7.  Exhibit F records that on 02/15/2018 you attended an exit interview and, according to SkyVault's IT notes, declined to return or identify the USB device. Tell me what happened at that exit interview, what you were asked to return, what you did with the device and any copies, and whether you have ever certified the deletion or destruction of SkyVault material.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, Row #46 (ADMIN_NOTE dated 02/15/2018: "Exit interview for M. Holt completed by HR. Employee declined to return or identify USB device. Laptop SV-ENG-WS-014 retained by IT for forensic imaging") and Row #40 (exit interview scheduled 02/15/2018, IT to preserve logs and endpoint data per litigation hold); skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 52 (alleging Holt did not return the USB device or the files and did not certify destruction of copies) and 50 (citing Exhibit F for the bulk download event); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 3.5(a)-(c) (duty to return Company Materials, permanently delete or destroy electronic copies on personal devices, accounts or media, and certify compliance in writing) and 4.4 (exit procedures and separation certification).

Evidentiary purpose: This is the highest-exposure question in the Holt interview and the one on which the breach-of-contract count (Complaint paras. 128(a), 128(b)) most directly turns, because Section 3.5 requires an affirmative written certification that Holt must either produce or explain. The question also establishes whether the device and any copies still exist, which governs the practicality of any return, deletion or forensic examination and therefore the scope of injunctive relief that could be stipulated to later. Because Holt is a party to the ECIAA, counsel should complete a conflicts check before this line of questioning and should not press for a legal characterization of Section 3.5 during the interview.

Q-A8.  Describe your departure from SkyVault and your founding of Meridian — the date you resigned, your last day, the date Meridian was formed, who else was involved, and when you began technical work on what became PathForge.

Source: skyvault-complaint.docx paras. 2 (alleging departure and co-founding approximately two months later), 43 (alleging resignation effective February 16, 2018), 53 (alleging incorporation on or about April 11, 2018 with Priya Chandrasekaran and Holt's assumption of the CTO role) and 9 (alleging Meridian formed April 11, 2018); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Sections 7.1(a)-(b) (twelve-month non-solicitation period measured from termination of employment, including a six-month lookback on hiring former SkyVault employees); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, Section 1 ("Developed from the ground up beginning in 2018") and Section 7.2 first timeline bullet (April 2018: Meridian Dynamics, Inc. incorporated in Delaware; PathForge development begins under Dr. Marcus Holt's technical leadership).

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the chronology that the Complaint uses to argue that the speed of PathForge development is "consistent with" misappropriation (Complaint paras. 54 and 140). The interview should pin down the gap between the last day of SkyVault employment and the first day of PathForge technical work, because that interval is the most readily testable element of the Plaintiff's inference and the one Meridian's own records can corroborate. It also develops the facts relevant to ECIAA Section 7.1, which the Complaint does not plead as a breach but which the Plaintiff could add by amendment.

Q-A9.  Who joined Meridian from SkyVault, when, and what roles did they take; and describe how you handled recruiting and hiring in the twelve months after you left SkyVault.

Counsel should confirm at the outset that each witness has been told the interview is privileged, that they should not speculate, and that an "I don't recall" or "I would need to check the repository" answer is more useful than a confident reconstruction.

Q-C12.  Was any internal investigation, factual review or technical assessment commissioned after March 2024, and if so, who conducted it, what was it asked to determine, and what did it produce?

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes the existence, authorship and custody of any internal assessment, which is a threshold fact for the privilege analysis in Track 2 and for determining whether the assessment is a business review, an attorney-directed work-product analysis, or both. The question asks only what was commissioned and produced as a factual matter; the content and protection of the assessment are addressed in Track 2.

C.2 — TRACK 2: THE PRIVILEGE AND WORK-PRODUCT BOUNDARY

Counsel should open Track 2 by stating, on the record, that the discussion is for the purpose of obtaining legal advice and identifying protected material, and should document that statement. The questions below are designed to separate discoverable factual events from communications, legal opinions and attorney mental impressions that may be protected. Track 2 should not be conducted until Track 1 is complete.

Q-C13.  For the March-April 2024 period, identify by date, sender, recipient and subject matter the communications that were made for the purpose of obtaining or providing legal advice, and identify separately the communications that were ordinary business communications about the same events.

Evidentiary purpose: Constructs the privilege log architecture before any production is negotiated, and identifies the line between legal advice and business conduct. The distinction matters because the underlying events — receipt of the letter, the decision to retain counsel, the decision to decline the audit demand, the offer to negotiate — are discoverable, while the advice about them may not be. This question is the foundation for every privilege assertion Meridian will make in this matter.

Q-C14.  Identify any documents created in anticipation of litigation — analyses, chronologies, technical reviews, claim assessments, damages models, interview memoranda — and tell me who created each, when, at whose direction, and for what purpose.

Evidentiary purpose: Identifies work-product material by document, author, date and direction so that protection can be asserted and maintained. Documents created because of anticipated litigation are treated differently from documents created in the ordinary course, and the distinction can only be drawn if the creating circumstances are documented now, while the authors are available and before any production is discussed.

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes a consistent and defensible approach to mixed documents before a production protocol is negotiated, and reduces the risk of inadvertent waiver. The April 5 Response is itself an example of a dual-purpose document, which makes it a useful concrete reference point for testing whether Meridian's stated practice matches how it actually handles such material.

IX. RECOMMENDED INTERVIEW SEQUENCE AND HOW IT TESTS LATER WITNESS ACCOUNTS

No single order is correct for every case, and the recommendation below should be revisited once the first two interviews are complete and once the initial document collections have been returned. The order that best fits the present record, the privilege posture and the available documents is as follows.

First: the Meridian legal lead, Track 1 only (Questions C-1 through C-12). This category should go first for three reasons. The legal lead can fix the discoverable chronology of the March-April 2024 response, which is the predicate for the willfulness allegations and the earliest-litigated preservation issues, and that chronology does not depend on any technical witness. The legal lead can also identify, before any other interview is scheduled, which Meridian personnel hold responsive documents and which have already been asked to prepare factual accounts — information that determines who else must be interviewed and in what order. Finally, Track 1 lets counsel map the privilege boundary from the inside before speaking to witnesses whose recollections could otherwise be shaped by an incomplete understanding of what is protected. Track 2 (Questions C-13 through C-18) should be completed with the same witness once Track 1 is documented, and before any technical interview is conducted.

Second: Dr. Holt (Questions A-1 through A-32), after the conflicts check described at Q-A7 has been completed. Holt should be second because he is the only witness who can provide the connecting account across all six lead families, and because his interview produces the specific document requests — repositories, design records, the F:\SkyVault_Export\ destination and the SanDisk device identifier from Exhibit F, and the white paper drafting file — that the technical interviews and the collections will then be organized around. Taking Holt's account second, while the legal lead's chronology is fresh, allows counsel to test his recollection of the 2024 correspondence against the documented routing chain rather than accepting it in isolation.

Third and subsequently: the Meridian technical team, module by module (Questions B-1 through B-15), beginning with the witness who worked on the module most directly implicated by the Complaint's claim charts. The technical interviews come last because they are the cross-check. By that point counsel will have the legal lead's document map, Holt's account, and the first returned collections, so each engineer can be asked to confirm or contradict a specific proposition rather than to reconstruct history from memory. The order within this category should follow the modules: multi-sensor fusion first, because the Complaint's '561 Patent claim chart is the most developed and the white paper's Section 3 is the most detailed; GPS-denied navigation and adaptive path optimization second, because that is where the DroneNav provenance question and the '227 Patent overlap; and swarm coordination third, because the white paper itself dates that module to 2019 with production deployment in 2021 and the '889 Patent was filed June 22, 2020, making its chronology the most easily tested against release records.

How this sequence tests later accounts. Sequencing the interviews this way turns each later interview into a verification step against an already-documented record. The legal lead's chronology is tested against Holt's recollection of the same events and against the written hold and routing records, so any divergence is visible immediately rather than at a deposition. Holt's account of what he took, retained and used (Q-A6, Q-A7, Q-A21, Q-A32) is tested against Exhibit F's row-level event data, against the SanDisk device identifier and the F:\SkyVault_Export\ destination path, and against the technical witnesses' systems-level answer at Q-B5. Holt's account of the PathForge starting point and timeline (Q-A10, Q-A15 to Q-A18) is tested against repository commit metadata, release records and the engineers' own module histories at Q-B1, Q-B2 and Q-B12 — records that were created contemporaneously and that do not depend on anyone's memory. The white paper's provenance claims (Q-A22 to Q-A28) are tested against the engineers' source-by-source answers at Q-B6 through Q-B9 and against the dependency and license records, which will show whether the four published references reflect actual use or only citation. And the independent-development and compliance representations in the April 5 Response (Q-C5, Q-C6) are tested last, against everything collected, so that Meridian knows before it repeats those representations in a filing whether they are supported, need qualification, or need to be withdrawn.

Two practical cautions apply to the sequence. First, if the legal lead's Track 1 answers show that preservation steps were incomplete or that responsive records have been lost, that issue should be addressed with counsel before any further interviews, because it changes the risk profile of every subsequent session. Second, if the technical interviews produce an account that differs materially from Holt's, counsel should not attempt to reconcile the two in the same session; the divergence should be documented and the affected questions re-asked after the records are collected.
